1	"""State machine for trajectory execution lifecycle.
2	
3	Provides a reusable :class:`TrajectoryExecutionMachine` that encapsulates the
4	state handling logic shared across movement controllers (``move_forward``,
5	``TrajectoryCursor``, …).
6	
7	The machine processes :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState` updates and
8	determines trajectory execution state transitions — including forward/backward
9	movement, pauses and trajectory completion — in a single, testable place.
10	
11	State diagram (``ss`` = standstill)::
12	
13	    idle ──start──→ armed ──RUNNING──→ executing
14	                      │                   │
15	                      │ parked PAUSED_BY_USER, stale terminal: stay
16	                      │
17	    executing ──ended+ss──→ ended        executing ──paused+ss──→ paused
18	    executing ──ended─────→ ending ──ss──→ ended
19	    executing ──paused────→ pausing ──ss──→ paused
20	
21	    ending / pausing ──RUNNING──→ executing      (never settled)
22	    pausing ──ended──→ ending | ended            (pause overran the end)
23	
24	    paused(IO)   ──RUNNING──→ executing          (observed resume)
25	    paused(USER) ──RUNNING──→ error              (no start was issued)
26	    ended        ──RUNNING──→ error
27	
28	    paused / ended ──start──→ armed
29	
30	    Any state may transition to ``error`` via :meth:`fail`.
31	
32	Three regimes decide how a frame is read:
33	
34	* **armed** — a start was issued but the robot has not moved yet. The
35	  controller publishes the *parked* shape (``PAUSED_BY_USER`` at standstill,
36	  level-based since robotics/wbr!2262) from initialization until motion begins,
37	  and re-publishes the terminal state a resume was started out of
38	  (``PAUSED_ON_IO``, ``END_OF_TRAJECTORY``) for a few cycles. Neither is a
39	  pause or a completion; ``armed`` waits for ``RUNNING``. Only a pause this
40	  machine was told about (:meth:`request_pause`), a parked frame after the
41	  robot was seen leaving standstill, or a fresh IO pause are real pauses here.
42	* **transient** (``ending`` / ``pausing``) — a terminal discriminator was seen
43	  while the robot was still moving; standstill concludes it. A ``RUNNING``
44	  frame in a transient state means the controller never settled (a stale
45	  pause frame at motion start, or a re-armed execution) and returns the
46	  machine to ``executing``: waiting for standstill would either hang or
47	  conclude the wrong thing at the next standstill flicker.
48	* **rest** (``paused`` / ``ended``) — the operation is resolved and standstill
49	  was confirmed. ``RUNNING`` here without a start from this machine is a
50	  contradiction: for a user pause or a finished trajectory the machine goes to
51	  ``error`` with :attr:`failure_reason` set (nobody but this cursor may resume
52	  or restart), for an IO pause it follows the wire (a controller that resumes
53	  an IO pause by itself is conceivable, ADR 002).
54	
55	The consumer guarantees that :meth:`arm` (``start``) is sent *before* the frame
56	that follows a new movement command is processed; "still at rest when RUNNING
57	arrives" therefore means "no start was issued".
58	
59	The ``ss`` edges out of ``ending`` and ``pausing`` fire on any standstill
60	frame, **with or without an ``execute`` block**: RAE publishes the execute
61	state level-based, but controllers older than wbr!2262 drop the block the
62	instant the robot settles, leaving bare standstill frames as the only
63	completion signal. A bare standstill never concludes anything from ``armed``
64	or ``executing`` — without a terminal discriminator there is nothing to
65	conclude. See this package's README for the full wire behaviour.
66	
67	Example::
68	
69	    machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
70	    machine.arm()
71	
72	    async for state in motion_group_states:
73	        result = machine.process_motion_state(state)
74	
75	        if result.location is not None:
76	            update_location(result.location)
77	
78	        if machine.is_error:
79	            raise RuntimeError(machine.failure_reason)
80	        if machine.is_ended:
81	            break
82	        if machine.is_paused:
83	            handle_pause()
84	"""
85	
86	from __future__ import annotations
87	
88	import logging
89	from dataclasses import dataclass
90	from enum import Enum, auto
91	
92	from statemachine import State, StateMachine
93	
94	from nova import api
95	
96	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
97	
98	_TERMINAL_STATES = (
99	    api.models.TrajectoryEnded,
100	    api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser,
101	    api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO,
102	)
103	
104	
105	class PauseReason(Enum):
106	    """Why the controller holds an execution in ``pausing``/``paused``.
107	
108	    ``USER``: a ``PauseMovementRequest`` (or a stopped execution — the wire has no
109	    separate kind for it). ``IO``: the ``pause_on_io`` condition attached to the
110	    start became true. Both are resumed with a new ``StartMovementRequest``; the
111	    controller never resumes an IO pause by itself, even after the condition
112	    clears (measured 2026-09-03, see
113	    docs/architecture/incoming/pause-on-signal-evaluation.md).
114	    """
115	
116	    USER = auto()
117	    IO = auto()
118	
119	
120	TrajectoryState = (
121	    api.models.TrajectoryRunning
122	    | api.models.TrajectoryEnded
123	    | api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
124	    | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO
125	    | api.models.TrajectoryWaitForIO
126	    | None
127	)
128	
129	
130	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
131	# Result type returned by process_motion_state
132	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
133	
134	
135	@dataclass(frozen=True)
136	class StateUpdate:
137	    """Result of processing a single :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState`.
138	
139	    Attributes:
140	        location: Updated trajectory location (``None`` when no
141	            :class:`~nova.api.models.TrajectoryDetails` were present).
142	        has_execute: ``True`` when the ``execute`` field was set on the
143	            incoming :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState`.
144	        state_changed: ``True`` when the machine transitioned to a
145	            different state during this processing step.
146	        previous_state_id: Identifier of the state *before* this step.
147	        current_state_id: Identifier of the state *after* this step.
148	    """
149	
150	    location: float | None = None
151	    has_execute: bool = False
152	    state_changed: bool = False
153	    previous_state_id: str = ""
154	    current_state_id: str = ""
155	
156	    @property
157	    def skip(self) -> bool:
158	        """Convenience — ``True`` when the state carried no useful information."""
159	        return not self.has_execute and not self.state_changed
160	
161	
162	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
163	# State machine
164	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	
166	
167	class TrajectoryExecutionMachine(StateMachine):
168	    """Finite-state machine for a single trajectory execution lifecycle.
169	
170	    **States**
171	
172	    ============  =============================================================
173	    ``idle``       No trajectory active — waiting for :meth:`arm`.
174	    ``armed``      Start issued, robot not yet moving. The controller's parked
175	                   ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` frames and the re-published terminal
176	                   state of the stop a resume leaves (same kind, same
177	                   location) are expected here and change nothing.
178	    ``executing``  Robot is moving (``TrajectoryRunning``).
179	    ``ending``     ``TrajectoryEnded`` received but robot not yet at standstill.
180	    ``pausing``    ``TrajectoryPausedByUser`` or ``TrajectoryPausedOnIO``
181	                   received, not yet at standstill.
182	    ``paused``     Robot paused and at standstill — may :meth:`arm` again.
183	                   :attr:`pause_reason` tells a user pause from an IO pause.
184	    ``ended``      Trajectory finished **and** robot at standstill.
185	    ``error``      A frame contradicted the state the machine was in (see
186	                   :attr:`failure_reason`), or :meth:`fail` was called.
187	    ============  =============================================================
188	
189	    **External commands**
190	
191	    * :meth:`arm` (event ``start``) — begin (or resume) execution. A resume
192	      ignores frames repeating the terminal state it leaves until a different
193	      frame arrives, so they are not mistaken for a new completion.
194	    * :meth:`request_pause` — this machine's owner sent a pause request; the
195	      next parked-looking frame is a real pause even before the robot moved.
196	    * ``fail`` — signal an error from any non-terminal state.
197	
198	    All trajectory-state transitions are triggered internally by
199	    :meth:`process_motion_state`. The owner must send ``start`` for a new
200	    movement command *before* processing the frames that follow it; the
201	    rest-state rules rely on it.
202	    """
203	
204	    # -- States ---------------------------------------------------------------
205	
206	    idle = State(initial=True)
207	    armed = State()
208	    executing = State()
209	    ending = State()
210	    pausing = State()
211	    paused = State()
212	    ended = State()
213	    error = State(final=True)
214	
215	    # -- External commands ----------------------------------------------------
216	
217	    start = idle.to(armed) | paused.to(armed) | ended.to(armed)
218	
219	    fail = (
220	        idle.to(error)
221	        | armed.to(error)
222	        | executing.to(error)
223	        | ending.to(error)
224	        | pausing.to(error)
225	        | paused.to(error)
226	        | ended.to(error)
227	    )
228	
229	    # -- Internal transitions (triggered by process_motion_state) -------------
230	
231	    _keep_armed = armed.to(armed, internal=True)
232	    _begin_executing = armed.to(executing)
233	    _end_while_armed = armed.to(ended)
234	    _begin_ending_while_armed = armed.to(ending)
235	    _pause_while_armed = armed.to(paused)
236	    _begin_pausing_while_armed = armed.to(pausing)
237	
238	    _keep_executing = executing.to(executing, internal=True)
239	
240	    _end_immediately = executing.to(ended)
241	    _begin_ending = executing.to(ending)
242	
243	    _pause_immediately = executing.to(paused)
244	    _begin_pausing = executing.to(pausing)
245	
246	    _end_after_standstill = ending.to(ended)
247	    _keep_ending = ending.to(ending, internal=True)
248	    _resume_from_ending = ending.to(executing)
249	
250	    _pause_after_standstill = pausing.to(paused)
251	    _keep_pausing = pausing.to(pausing, internal=True)
252	    _resume_from_pausing = pausing.to(executing)
253	    _end_from_pausing = pausing.to(ended)
254	    _begin_ending_from_pausing = pausing.to(ending)
255	
256	    # An IO pause the controller resumed without a start from this machine
257	    # (another client, or a controller that clears it by itself): follow the wire.
258	    _resume_observed = paused.to(executing)
259	
260	    # -- Instance state -------------------------------------------------------
261	
262	    def __init__(self) -> None:
263	        self.location: float | None = None
264	        self.pause_reason: PauseReason | None = None
265	        self.failure_reason: str | None = None
266	        self.failed_frame: api.models.MotionGroupState | None = None
267	        self._moved = False
268	        self._pause_requested = False
269	        # (state kind, location) of the last terminal frame seen, and the one a
270	        # resume must ignore while the controller still re-publishes it.
271	        self._last_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
272	        self._stale_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
273	        super().__init__()
274	
275	    def _active_configuration_id(self) -> str:
276	        """String id for the active configuration (uses :attr:`StateChart.configuration`)."""
277	        cfg = self.configuration
278	        if not cfg:
279	            return ""
280	        if len(cfg) == 1:
281	            return next(iter(cfg)).id
282	        return ",".join(s.id for s in cfg)
283	
284	    # -- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------
285	
286	    def arm(self, *, pause_requested: bool = False, accept_repeated_terminal: bool = False) -> None:
287	        """Begin or resume execution (sends ``start``).
288	
289	        A start out of ``ended``/``paused`` ignores frames that repeat the terminal
290	        state it leaves — same kind at the same location — until any different
291	        frame arrives: level-based controllers keep re-publishing the previous
292	        stop until they take up the new command, and those frames belong to the
293	        old operation. A genuine new terminal state is always preceded by a
294	        different frame (``WAIT_FOR_IO`` or ``RUNNING``), which lifts the filter —
295	        including a start issued at the very end of the trajectory.
296	
297	        Args:
298	            pause_requested: The operation being armed for is itself a pause (the
299	                owner paused before the machine ever left rest), so the parked
300	                frame concludes it — see :meth:`request_pause`.
301	            accept_repeated_terminal: The owner knows the command has nowhere to
302	                go (a forward at the end, a backward at the start, a target equal
303	                to the current location): the repeated terminal state *is* the
304	                genuine outcome, so it concludes the operation at once instead of
305	                waiting for the controller's ``WAIT_FOR_IO`` to lift the filter.
306	        """
307	        self.send("start")
308	        self._pause_requested = pause_requested
309	        if accept_repeated_terminal:
310	            self._stale_terminal = None
311	
312	    def request_pause(self) -> None:
313	        """Record that the owner sent a pause request.
314	
315	        A ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` frame at standstill is then a real pause even while
316	        ``armed``, where it would otherwise be read as the parked pre-motion shape.
317	        """
318	        self._pause_requested = True
319	
320	    def process_motion_state(self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> StateUpdate:
321	        """Feed a :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState` into the machine.
322	
323	        This is the **main entry point** for movement controllers.  It
324	        inspects the incoming state, fires the appropriate internal
325	        transition and returns a :class:`StateUpdate` describing what
326	        happened.
327	
328	        Args:
329	            state: The latest motion-group state from the API stream.
330	
331	        Returns:
332	            A :class:`StateUpdate` with location, execute presence and
333	            transition information.
334	        """
335	        previous_state_id: str = self._active_configuration_id()
336	        has_execute = state.execute is not None
337	        location: float | None = None
338	
339	        if not has_execute:
340	            # No execute details on this frame. Current controllers drop the
341	            # trajectory `execute` block the instant the robot settles
342	            # (robotics/wbr MotionPointGenerator removes the provider on
343	            # END_OF_TRAJECTORY/USER_PAUSED, not only on STOPPED — slated to
344	            # change with wbr!2262), so a bare standstill can be the only
345	            # completion signal we ever receive. When we are already waiting
346	            # for standstill (`ending` / `pausing`), honour it: the
347	            # discriminator was already seen on the transition into that
348	            # state. Otherwise there is nothing to conclude from the frame.
349	            if state.standstill:
350	                if self.current_state == self.ending:
351	                    self._end_after_standstill()
352	                elif self.current_state == self.pausing:
353	                    self._pause_after_standstill()
354	            current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
355	            return StateUpdate(
356	                has_execute=False,
357	                state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
358	                previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
359	                current_state_id=current_id,
360	            )
361	
362	        # Execute *is* present ------------------------------------------------
363	        assert state.execute is not None  # mypy
364	        if isinstance(state.execute.details, api.models.TrajectoryDetails):
365	            location = state.execute.details.location
366	            self.location = location
367	            trajectory_state = state.execute.details.state
368	
369	            terminal = (
370	                (type(trajectory_state), location)
371	                if isinstance(trajectory_state, _TERMINAL_STATES)
372	                else None
373	            )
374	            if self._stale_terminal is not None:
375	                # A pause the owner requested is concluded by the very frame a
376	                # resume would otherwise ignore.
377	                requested_pause = self._pause_requested and isinstance(
378	                    trajectory_state, api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
379	                )
380	                if terminal == self._stale_terminal and not requested_pause:
381	                    if self.current_state == self.armed:
382	                        self._keep_armed()
383	                    current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
384	                    return StateUpdate(
385	                        location=location,
386	                        has_execute=True,
387	                        state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
388	                        previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
389	                        current_state_id=current_id,
390	                    )
391	                # Anything else proves the controller has moved on from the
392	                # terminal state the current start was issued out of.
393	                self._stale_terminal = None
394	            if terminal is not None:
395	                self._last_terminal = terminal
396	
397	            if self.current_state == self.armed:
398	                self._handle_armed(trajectory_state, state)
399	            elif self.current_state == self.executing:
400	                self._handle_executing(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
401	            elif self.current_state == self.ending:
402	                self._handle_ending(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
403	            elif self.current_state == self.pausing:
404	                self._handle_pausing(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
405	            elif self.current_state in (self.paused, self.ended):
406	                self._handle_at_rest(trajectory_state, state)
407	
408	        current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
409	        return StateUpdate(
410	            location=location,
411	            has_execute=True,
412	            state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
413	            previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
414	            current_state_id=current_id,
415	        )
416	
417	    # -- Convenience properties -----------------------------------------------
418	
419	    @property
420	    def is_idle(self) -> bool:
421	        return self.current_state == self.idle
422	
423	    @property
424	    def is_armed(self) -> bool:
425	        return self.current_state == self.armed
426	
427	    @property
428	    def is_executing(self) -> bool:
429	        return self.current_state == self.executing
430	
431	    @property
432	    def is_ending(self) -> bool:
433	        return self.current_state == self.ending
434	
435	    @property
436	    def is_pausing(self) -> bool:
437	        return self.current_state == self.pausing
438	
439	    @property
440	    def is_paused(self) -> bool:
441	        return self.current_state == self.paused
442	
443	    @property
444	    def is_paused_on_io(self) -> bool:
445	        """``True`` while the controller holds an IO pause (``pausing`` or ``paused``)."""
446	        return (
447	            self.current_state in (self.pausing, self.paused)
448	            and self.pause_reason is PauseReason.IO
449	        )
450	
451	    @property
452	    def is_ended(self) -> bool:
453	        return self.current_state == self.ended
454	
455	    @property
456	    def is_error(self) -> bool:
457	        return self.current_state == self.error
458	
459	    @property
460	    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
461	        """``True`` when in a final state (ended or error)."""
462	        return self.current_state in (self.ended, self.error)
463	
464	    @property
465	    def is_waiting_for_standstill(self) -> bool:
466	        """``True`` when trajectory ended or paused but robot still decelerating."""
467	        return self.current_state in (self.ending, self.pausing)
468	
469	    # -- Logging callbacks (python-statemachine hooks) ------------------------
470	
471	    def on_start(self, source: State) -> None:
472	        # Level-based publishing (robotics/wbr!2262) keeps re-publishing the
473	        # terminal state of the previous stop until the controller has taken up
474	        # the new command. Resuming from `ended`/`paused` therefore first sees
475	        # the old END_OF_TRAJECTORY / PAUSED_* frames again; concluding the new
476	        # operation from them would report it finished at its start. They are
477	        # told apart from a genuine new terminal state by identity: same kind at
478	        # the same location as the state we are leaving.
479	        self._stale_terminal = self._last_terminal if source in (self.ended, self.paused) else None
480	
481	    def on_enter_armed(self) -> None:
482	        self._moved = False
483	        self._pause_requested = False
484	        self.pause_reason = None
485	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → armed (waiting for motion)")
486	
487	    def on_enter_executing(self) -> None:
488	        self.pause_reason = None
489	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → executing")
490	
491	    def on_enter_ending(self) -> None:
492	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → ending (waiting for standstill)")
493	
494	    def on_enter_pausing(self) -> None:
495	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → pausing (waiting for standstill)")
496	
497	    def on_enter_paused(self) -> None:
498	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → paused (%s)", self.pause_reason)
499	
500	    def on_enter_ended(self) -> None:
501	        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → ended")
502	
503	    def on_enter_error(self) -> None:
504	        logger.error("Trajectory state machine → error: %s", self.failure_reason)
505	
506	    # -- Private helpers ------------------------------------------------------
507	
508	    def _handle_armed(
509	        self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, state: api.models.MotionGroupState
510	    ) -> None:
511	        """Wait for motion; the parked shape is a no-op (stale terminals never get here)."""
512	        standstill = state.standstill
513	        match trajectory_state:
514	            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
515	                self._begin_executing()
516	
517	            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
518	                if standstill:
519	                    self._end_while_armed()
520	                else:
521	                    self._begin_ending_while_armed()
522	
523	            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
524	                # No parked look-alike exists for PAUSED_ON_IO: the controller only
525	                # reports it after a start armed with pause_on_io, also when the
526	                # condition already held at the start and the robot never moved.
527	                self.pause_reason = PauseReason.IO
528	                if standstill:
529	                    self._pause_while_armed()
530	                else:
531	                    self._begin_pausing_while_armed()
532	
533	            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser():
534	                if not standstill:
535	                    # The robot is leaving standstill; the discriminator flips to
536	                    # RUNNING one cycle later (measured 2026-09-16).
537	                    self._moved = True
538	                    self._keep_armed()
539	                elif self._moved or self._pause_requested:
540	                    self.pause_reason = PauseReason.USER

542	                else:
543	                    # The parked pre-motion shape (robotics/wbr!2262).
544	                    self._keep_armed()
545	
546	            case _:
547	                # WAIT_FOR_IO (start_on_io holding the robot) / unknown: not moving yet.
548	                self._keep_armed()
549	
550	    def _handle_executing(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
551	        """Determine the right transition while in ``executing`` state."""
552	        match trajectory_state:
553	            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
554	                if standstill:
555	                    self._end_immediately()
556	                else:
557	                    self._begin_ending()
558	
559	            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
560	                # An IO pause is a suspended execution, not completion: the
561	                # controller holds it (level-based, re-published every step) until
562	                # a new start arrives. Treating it as ``ended`` made execute()
563	                # return mid-trajectory (docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md).
564	                self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
565	                if standstill:
566	                    self._pause_immediately()
567	                else:
568	                    self._begin_pausing()
569	
570	            case _:
571	                # RUNNING / WAIT_FOR_IO / unknown — stay executing. A standstill
572	                # flag on a RUNNING frame is jitter, not a completion.
573	                self._keep_executing()
574	
575	    def _handle_ending(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
576	        match trajectory_state:
577	            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
578	                logger.warning(
579	                    "Controller reports RUNNING at location %s while the trajectory was ending; "
580	                    "resuming execution tracking",
581	                    self.location,
582	                )
583	                self._resume_from_ending()
584	            case _:
585	                if standstill:
586	                    self._end_after_standstill()
587	                else:
588	                    self._keep_ending()
589	
590	    def _handle_pausing(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
591	        match trajectory_state:
592	            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
593	                # The pause never settled: a stale PAUSED_BY_USER at motion start,
594	                # or the controller re-armed. Waiting for standstill here would
595	                # hang, or conclude a "pause" at the next standstill flicker.
596	                self._resume_from_pausing()
597	            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
598	                if standstill:
599	                    self._end_from_pausing()
600	                else:
601	                    self._begin_ending_from_pausing()
602	            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
603	                self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
604	                if standstill:
605	                    self._pause_after_standstill()
606	                else:
607	                    self._keep_pausing()
608	            case _:
609	                if standstill:
610	                    self._pause_after_standstill()
611	                else:
612	                    self._keep_pausing()
613	
614	    def _handle_at_rest(
615	        self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, state: api.models.MotionGroupState
616	    ) -> None:
617	        """``paused`` / ``ended``: the owner sends ``start`` before any frame of a new movement."""
618	        if self.current_state == self.paused:
619	            match trajectory_state:
620	                case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():

625	                case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():

627	                    # (re)starts being evaluated while the robot stands, e.g.
628	                    # after the bus-IO service came back (measured).
629	                    self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
630	                case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
631	                    logger.warning(
632	                        "Controller reports END_OF_TRAJECTORY at location %s while paused",
633	                        self.location,
634	                    )
635	        else:
636	            match trajectory_state:
637	                case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
638	                    self._fail_on_frame(state, trajectory_state)
639	                case api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
640	                    logger.warning(
641	                        "Controller reports PAUSED_ON_IO at location %s after the trajectory ended",
642	                        self.location,
643	                    )
644	
645	    def _fail_on_frame(
646	        self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState
647	    ) -> None:
648	        self.failure_reason = (
649	            f"controller reports {type(trajectory_state).__name__} at location {self.location} "
650	            f"(standstill={state.standstill}) while the execution is "
651	            f"'{self._active_configuration_id()}' "
652	            "and no start was issued"
653	        )
654	        self.failed_frame = state
655	        self.fail()
656	
657	    @staticmethod
658	    def _reason_of(trajectory_state: TrajectoryState) -> PauseReason:
659	        return (
660	            PauseReason.IO
661	            if isinstance(trajectory_state, api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO)

"""State machine for trajectory execution lifecycle.

Provides a reusable :class:`TrajectoryExecutionMachine` that encapsulates the
state handling logic shared across movement controllers (``move_forward``,
``TrajectoryCursor``, …).

The machine processes :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState` updates and
determines trajectory execution state transitions — including forward/backward
movement, pauses and trajectory completion — in a single, testable place.

State diagram (``ss`` = standstill)::

    idle ──start──→ armed ──RUNNING──→ executing
                      │                   │
                      │ parked PAUSED_BY_USER, stale terminal: stay
                      │
    executing ──ended+ss──→ ended        executing ──paused+ss──→ paused
    executing ──ended─────→ ending ──ss──→ ended
    executing ──paused────→ pausing ──ss──→ paused

    ending / pausing ──RUNNING──→ executing      (never settled)
    pausing ──ended──→ ending | ended            (pause overran the end)

    paused(IO)   ──RUNNING──→ executing          (observed resume)
    paused(USER) ──RUNNING──→ error              (no start was issued)
    ended        ──RUNNING──→ error

    paused / ended ──start──→ armed

    Any state may transition to ``error`` via :meth:`fail`.

Three regimes decide how a frame is read:

* **armed** — a start was issued but the robot has not moved yet. The
  controller publishes the *parked* shape (``PAUSED_BY_USER`` at standstill,
  level-based since robotics/wbr!2262) from initialization until motion begins,
  and re-publishes the terminal state a resume was started out of
  (``PAUSED_ON_IO``, ``END_OF_TRAJECTORY``) for a few cycles. Neither is a
  pause or a completion; ``armed`` waits for ``RUNNING``. Only a pause this
  machine was told about (:meth:`request_pause`), a parked frame after the
  robot was seen leaving standstill, or a fresh IO pause are real pauses here.
* **transient** (``ending`` / ``pausing``) — a terminal discriminator was seen
  while the robot was still moving; standstill concludes it. A ``RUNNING``
  frame in a transient state means the controller never settled (a stale
  pause frame at motion start, or a re-armed execution) and returns the
  machine to ``executing``: waiting for standstill would either hang or
  conclude the wrong thing at the next standstill flicker.
* **rest** (``paused`` / ``ended``) — the operation is resolved and standstill
  was confirmed. ``RUNNING`` here without a start from this machine is a
  contradiction: for a user pause or a finished trajectory the machine goes to
  ``error`` with :attr:`failure_reason` set (nobody but this cursor may resume
  or restart), for an IO pause it follows the wire (a controller that resumes
  an IO pause by itself is conceivable, ADR 002).

The consumer guarantees that :meth:`arm` (``start``) is sent *before* the frame
that follows a new movement command is processed; "still at rest when RUNNING
arrives" therefore means "no start was issued".

The ``ss`` edges out of ``ending`` and ``pausing`` fire on any standstill
frame, **with or without an ``execute`` block**: RAE publishes the execute
state level-based, but controllers older than wbr!2262 drop the block the
instant the robot settles, leaving bare standstill frames as the only
completion signal. A bare standstill never concludes anything from ``armed``
or ``executing`` — without a terminal discriminator there is nothing to
conclude. See this package's README for the full wire behaviour.

Example::

    machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
    machine.arm()

    async for state in motion_group_states:
        result = machine.process_motion_state(state)

        if result.location is not None:
            update_location(result.location)

        if machine.is_error:
            raise RuntimeError(machine.failure_reason)
        if machine.is_ended:
            break
        if machine.is_paused:
            handle_pause()
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum, auto

from statemachine import State, StateMachine

from nova import api

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_TERMINAL_STATES = (
    api.models.TrajectoryEnded,
    api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser,
    api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO,
)


class PauseReason(Enum):
    """Why the controller holds an execution in ``pausing``/``paused``.

    ``USER``: a ``PauseMovementRequest`` (or a stopped execution — the wire has no
    separate kind for it). ``IO``: the ``pause_on_io`` condition attached to the
    start became true. Both are resumed with a new ``StartMovementRequest``; the
    controller never resumes an IO pause by itself, even after the condition
    clears (measured 2026-09-03, see
    docs/architecture/incoming/pause-on-signal-evaluation.md).
    """

    USER = auto()
    IO = auto()


TrajectoryState = (
    api.models.TrajectoryRunning
    | api.models.TrajectoryEnded
    | api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
    | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO
    | api.models.TrajectoryWaitForIO
    | None
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Result type returned by process_motion_state
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StateUpdate:
    """Result of processing a single :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState`.

    Attributes:
        location: Updated trajectory location (``None`` when no
            :class:`~nova.api.models.TrajectoryDetails` were present).
        has_execute: ``True`` when the ``execute`` field was set on the
            incoming :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState`.
        state_changed: ``True`` when the machine transitioned to a
            different state during this processing step.
        previous_state_id: Identifier of the state *before* this step.
        current_state_id: Identifier of the state *after* this step.
    """

    location: float | None = None
    has_execute: bool = False
    state_changed: bool = False
    previous_state_id: str = ""
    current_state_id: str = ""

    @property
    def skip(self) -> bool:
        """Convenience — ``True`` when the state carried no useful information."""
        return not self.has_execute and not self.state_changed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# State machine
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TrajectoryExecutionMachine(StateMachine):
    """Finite-state machine for a single trajectory execution lifecycle.

    **States**

    ============  =============================================================
    ``idle``       No trajectory active — waiting for :meth:`arm`.
    ``armed``      Start issued, robot not yet moving. The controller's parked
                   ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` frames and the re-published terminal
                   state of the stop a resume leaves (same kind, same
                   location) are expected here and change nothing.
    ``executing``  Robot is moving (``TrajectoryRunning``).
    ``ending``     ``TrajectoryEnded`` received but robot not yet at standstill.
    ``pausing``    ``TrajectoryPausedByUser`` or ``TrajectoryPausedOnIO``
                   received, not yet at standstill.
    ``paused``     Robot paused and at standstill — may :meth:`arm` again.
                   :attr:`pause_reason` tells a user pause from an IO pause.
    ``ended``      Trajectory finished **and** robot at standstill.
    ``error``      A frame contradicted the state the machine was in (see
                   :attr:`failure_reason`), or :meth:`fail` was called.
    ============  =============================================================

    **External commands**

    * :meth:`arm` (event ``start``) — begin (or resume) execution. A resume
      ignores frames repeating the terminal state it leaves until a different
      frame arrives, so they are not mistaken for a new completion.
    * :meth:`request_pause` — this machine's owner sent a pause request; the
      next parked-looking frame is a real pause even before the robot moved.
    * ``fail`` — signal an error from any non-terminal state.

    All trajectory-state transitions are triggered internally by
    :meth:`process_motion_state`. The owner must send ``start`` for a new
    movement command *before* processing the frames that follow it; the
    rest-state rules rely on it.
    """

    # -- States ---------------------------------------------------------------

    idle = State(initial=True)
    armed = State()
    executing = State()
    ending = State()
    pausing = State()
    paused = State()
    ended = State()
    error = State(final=True)

    # -- External commands ----------------------------------------------------

    start = idle.to(armed) | paused.to(armed) | ended.to(armed)

    fail = (
        idle.to(error)
        | armed.to(error)
        | executing.to(error)
        | ending.to(error)
        | pausing.to(error)
        | paused.to(error)
        | ended.to(error)
    )

    # -- Internal transitions (triggered by process_motion_state) -------------

    _keep_armed = armed.to(armed, internal=True)
    _begin_executing = armed.to(executing)
    _end_while_armed = armed.to(ended)
    _begin_ending_while_armed = armed.to(ending)
    _pause_while_armed = armed.to(paused)
    _begin_pausing_while_armed = armed.to(pausing)

    _keep_executing = executing.to(executing, internal=True)

    _end_immediately = executing.to(ended)
    _begin_ending = executing.to(ending)

    _pause_immediately = executing.to(paused)
    _begin_pausing = executing.to(pausing)

    _end_after_standstill = ending.to(ended)
    _keep_ending = ending.to(ending, internal=True)
    _resume_from_ending = ending.to(executing)

    _pause_after_standstill = pausing.to(paused)
    _keep_pausing = pausing.to(pausing, internal=True)
    _resume_from_pausing = pausing.to(executing)
    _end_from_pausing = pausing.to(ended)
    _begin_ending_from_pausing = pausing.to(ending)

    # An IO pause the controller resumed without a start from this machine
    # (another client, or a controller that clears it by itself): follow the wire.
    _resume_observed = paused.to(executing)

    # -- Instance state -------------------------------------------------------

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.location: float | None = None
        self.pause_reason: PauseReason | None = None
        self.failure_reason: str | None = None
        self.failed_frame: api.models.MotionGroupState | None = None
        self._moved = False
        self._pause_requested = False
        # (state kind, location) of the last terminal frame seen, and the one a
        # resume must ignore while the controller still re-publishes it.
        self._last_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
        self._stale_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
        super().__init__()

    def _active_configuration_id(self) -> str:
        """String id for the active configuration (uses :attr:`StateChart.configuration`)."""
        cfg = self.configuration
        if not cfg:
            return ""
        if len(cfg) == 1:
            return next(iter(cfg)).id
        return ",".join(s.id for s in cfg)

    # -- Public API -----------------------------------------------------------

    def arm(self, *, pause_requested: bool = False, accept_repeated_terminal: bool = False) -> None:
        """Begin or resume execution (sends ``start``).

        A start out of ``ended``/``paused`` ignores frames that repeat the terminal
        state it leaves — same kind at the same location — until any different
        frame arrives: level-based controllers keep re-publishing the previous
        stop until they take up the new command, and those frames belong to the
        old operation. A genuine new terminal state is always preceded by a
        different frame (``WAIT_FOR_IO`` or ``RUNNING``), which lifts the filter —
        including a start issued at the very end of the trajectory.

        Args:
            pause_requested: The operation being armed for is itself a pause (the
                owner paused before the machine ever left rest), so the parked
                frame concludes it — see :meth:`request_pause`.
            accept_repeated_terminal: The owner knows the command has nowhere to
                go (a forward at the end, a backward at the start, a target equal
                to the current location): the repeated terminal state *is* the
                genuine outcome, so it concludes the operation at once instead of
                waiting for the controller's ``WAIT_FOR_IO`` to lift the filter.
        """
        self.send("start")
        self._pause_requested = pause_requested
        if accept_repeated_terminal:
            self._stale_terminal = None

    def request_pause(self) -> None:
        """Record that the owner sent a pause request.

        A ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` frame at standstill is then a real pause even while
        ``armed``, where it would otherwise be read as the parked pre-motion shape.
        """
        self._pause_requested = True

    def process_motion_state(self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> StateUpdate:
        """Feed a :class:`~nova.api.models.MotionGroupState` into the machine.

        This is the **main entry point** for movement controllers.  It
        inspects the incoming state, fires the appropriate internal
        transition and returns a :class:`StateUpdate` describing what
        happened.

        Args:
            state: The latest motion-group state from the API stream.

        Returns:
            A :class:`StateUpdate` with location, execute presence and
            transition information.
        """
        previous_state_id: str = self._active_configuration_id()
        has_execute = state.execute is not None
        location: float | None = None

        if not has_execute:
            # No execute details on this frame. Current controllers drop the
            # trajectory `execute` block the instant the robot settles
            # (robotics/wbr MotionPointGenerator removes the provider on
            # END_OF_TRAJECTORY/USER_PAUSED, not only on STOPPED — slated to
            # change with wbr!2262), so a bare standstill can be the only
            # completion signal we ever receive. When we are already waiting
            # for standstill (`ending` / `pausing`), honour it: the
            # discriminator was already seen on the transition into that
            # state. Otherwise there is nothing to conclude from the frame.
            if state.standstill:
                if self.current_state == self.ending:
                    self._end_after_standstill()
                elif self.current_state == self.pausing:
                    self._pause_after_standstill()
            current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
            return StateUpdate(
                has_execute=False,
                state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
                previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
                current_state_id=current_id,
            )

        # Execute *is* present ------------------------------------------------
        assert state.execute is not None  # mypy
        if isinstance(state.execute.details, api.models.TrajectoryDetails):
            location = state.execute.details.location
            self.location = location
            trajectory_state = state.execute.details.state

            terminal = (
                (type(trajectory_state), location)
                if isinstance(trajectory_state, _TERMINAL_STATES)
                else None
            )
            if self._stale_terminal is not None:
                # A pause the owner requested is concluded by the very frame a
                # resume would otherwise ignore.
                requested_pause = self._pause_requested and isinstance(
                    trajectory_state, api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
                )
                if terminal == self._stale_terminal and not requested_pause:
                    if self.current_state == self.armed:
                        self._keep_armed()
                    current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
                    return StateUpdate(
                        location=location,
                        has_execute=True,
                        state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
                        previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
                        current_state_id=current_id,
                    )
                # Anything else proves the controller has moved on from the
                # terminal state the current start was issued out of.
                self._stale_terminal = None
            if terminal is not None:
                self._last_terminal = terminal

            if self.current_state == self.armed:
                self._handle_armed(trajectory_state, state)
            elif self.current_state == self.executing:
                self._handle_executing(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
            elif self.current_state == self.ending:
                self._handle_ending(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
            elif self.current_state == self.pausing:
                self._handle_pausing(trajectory_state, standstill=state.standstill)
            elif self.current_state in (self.paused, self.ended):
                self._handle_at_rest(trajectory_state, state)

        current_id = self._active_configuration_id()
        return StateUpdate(
            location=location,
            has_execute=True,
            state_changed=current_id != previous_state_id,
            previous_state_id=previous_state_id,
            current_state_id=current_id,
        )

    # -- Convenience properties -----------------------------------------------

    @property
    def is_idle(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.idle

    @property
    def is_armed(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.armed

    @property
    def is_executing(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.executing

    @property
    def is_ending(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.ending

    @property
    def is_pausing(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.pausing

    @property
    def is_paused(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.paused

    @property
    def is_paused_on_io(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` while the controller holds an IO pause (``pausing`` or ``paused``)."""
        return (
            self.current_state in (self.pausing, self.paused)
            and self.pause_reason is PauseReason.IO
        )

    @property
    def is_ended(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.ended

    @property
    def is_error(self) -> bool:
        return self.current_state == self.error

    @property
    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when in a final state (ended or error)."""
        return self.current_state in (self.ended, self.error)

    @property
    def is_waiting_for_standstill(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when trajectory ended or paused but robot still decelerating."""
        return self.current_state in (self.ending, self.pausing)

    # -- Logging callbacks (python-statemachine hooks) ------------------------

    def on_start(self, source: State) -> None:
        # Level-based publishing (robotics/wbr!2262) keeps re-publishing the
        # terminal state of the previous stop until the controller has taken up
        # the new command. Resuming from `ended`/`paused` therefore first sees
        # the old END_OF_TRAJECTORY / PAUSED_* frames again; concluding the new
        # operation from them would report it finished at its start. They are
        # told apart from a genuine new terminal state by identity: same kind at
        # the same location as the state we are leaving.
        self._stale_terminal = self._last_terminal if source in (self.ended, self.paused) else None

    def on_enter_armed(self) -> None:
        self._moved = False
        self._pause_requested = False
        self.pause_reason = None
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → armed (waiting for motion)")

    def on_enter_executing(self) -> None:
        self.pause_reason = None
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → executing")

    def on_enter_ending(self) -> None:
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → ending (waiting for standstill)")

    def on_enter_pausing(self) -> None:
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → pausing (waiting for standstill)")

    def on_enter_paused(self) -> None:
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → paused (%s)", self.pause_reason)

    def on_enter_ended(self) -> None:
        logger.debug("Trajectory state machine → ended")

    def on_enter_error(self) -> None:
        logger.error("Trajectory state machine → error: %s", self.failure_reason)

    # -- Private helpers ------------------------------------------------------

    def _handle_armed(
        self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, state: api.models.MotionGroupState
    ) -> None:
        """Wait for motion; the parked shape is a no-op (stale terminals never get here)."""
        standstill = state.standstill
        match trajectory_state:
            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
                self._begin_executing()

            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
                if standstill:
                    self._end_while_armed()
                else:
                    self._begin_ending_while_armed()

            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
                # No parked look-alike exists for PAUSED_ON_IO: the controller only
                # reports it after a start armed with pause_on_io, also when the
                # condition already held at the start and the robot never moved.
                self.pause_reason = PauseReason.IO
                if standstill:
                    self._pause_while_armed()
                else:
                    self._begin_pausing_while_armed()

            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser():
                if not standstill:
                    # The robot is leaving standstill; the discriminator flips to
                    # RUNNING one cycle later (measured 2026-09-16).
                    self._moved = True
                    self._keep_armed()
                elif self._moved or self._pause_requested:
                    self.pause_reason = PauseReason.USER
                    self._pause_while_armed()
                else:
                    # The parked pre-motion shape (robotics/wbr!2262).
                    self._keep_armed()

            case _:
                # WAIT_FOR_IO (start_on_io holding the robot) / unknown: not moving yet.
                self._keep_armed()

    def _handle_executing(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
        """Determine the right transition while in ``executing`` state."""
        match trajectory_state:
            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
                if standstill:
                    self._end_immediately()
                else:
                    self._begin_ending()

            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
                # An IO pause is a suspended execution, not completion: the
                # controller holds it (level-based, re-published every step) until
                # a new start arrives. Treating it as ``ended`` made execute()
                # return mid-trajectory (docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md).
                self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
                if standstill:
                    self._pause_immediately()
                else:
                    self._begin_pausing()

            case _:
                # RUNNING / WAIT_FOR_IO / unknown — stay executing. A standstill
                # flag on a RUNNING frame is jitter, not a completion.
                self._keep_executing()

    def _handle_ending(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
        match trajectory_state:
            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
                logger.warning(
                    "Controller reports RUNNING at location %s while the trajectory was ending; "
                    "resuming execution tracking",
                    self.location,
                )
                self._resume_from_ending()
            case _:
                if standstill:
                    self._end_after_standstill()
                else:
                    self._keep_ending()

    def _handle_pausing(self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, *, standstill: bool) -> None:
        match trajectory_state:
            case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
                # The pause never settled: a stale PAUSED_BY_USER at motion start,
                # or the controller re-armed. Waiting for standstill here would
                # hang, or conclude a "pause" at the next standstill flicker.
                self._resume_from_pausing()
            case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
                if standstill:
                    self._end_from_pausing()
                else:
                    self._begin_ending_from_pausing()
            case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
                self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
                if standstill:
                    self._pause_after_standstill()
                else:
                    self._keep_pausing()
            case _:
                if standstill:
                    self._pause_after_standstill()
                else:
                    self._keep_pausing()

    def _handle_at_rest(
        self, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState, state: api.models.MotionGroupState
    ) -> None:
        """``paused`` / ``ended``: the owner sends ``start`` before any frame of a new movement."""
        if self.current_state == self.paused:
            match trajectory_state:
                case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
                    if self.pause_reason is PauseReason.IO:
                        self._resume_observed()
                    else:
                        self._fail_on_frame(state, trajectory_state)
                case api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser() | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
                    # A user pause turns into an IO pause when the condition
                    # (re)starts being evaluated while the robot stands, e.g.
                    # after the bus-IO service came back (measured).
                    self.pause_reason = self._reason_of(trajectory_state)
                case api.models.TrajectoryEnded():
                    logger.warning(
                        "Controller reports END_OF_TRAJECTORY at location %s while paused",
                        self.location,
                    )
        else:
            match trajectory_state:
                case api.models.TrajectoryRunning():
                    self._fail_on_frame(state, trajectory_state)
                case api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO():
                    logger.warning(
                        "Controller reports PAUSED_ON_IO at location %s after the trajectory ended",
                        self.location,
                    )

    def _fail_on_frame(
        self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState, trajectory_state: TrajectoryState
    ) -> None:
        self.failure_reason = (
            f"controller reports {type(trajectory_state).__name__} at location {self.location} "
            f"(standstill={state.standstill}) while the execution is "
            f"'{self._active_configuration_id()}' "
            "and no start was issued"
        )
        self.failed_frame = state
        self.fail()

    @staticmethod
    def _reason_of(trajectory_state: TrajectoryState) -> PauseReason:
        return (
            PauseReason.IO
            if isinstance(trajectory_state, api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO)
            else PauseReason.USER
        )

import asyncio
import contextlib
import logging

from nova.actions import MovementControllerContext
from nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_cursor import OperationResult, TrajectoryCursor
from nova.types import MovementControllerFunction

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def move_forward(context: MovementControllerContext) -> MovementControllerFunction:
    """Default movement controller: run the trajectory forward from start to end.

    This is a thin adapter over :class:`TrajectoryCursor`, which owns the
    ``executeTrajectory`` protocol; ``move_forward`` only configures a cursor for
    one-shot execution and starts it. The name and the plug-in seam
    (``MovementController`` / ``MovementControllerContext``) are kept for
    backwards compatibility.

    A controller-side IO pause (``context.pause_on_io``) suspends the movement
    without ending it: the controller holds the robot on path and waits for a
    new start, which it only honours once the condition has cleared. This
    adapter waits for that through ``context.wait_for_pause_on_io_release`` and
    starts again, as often as the signal comes and goes, until the trajectory is
    traversed — so ``execute()`` blocks through every pause and returns at the
    target. If the signal's source itself goes away
    (``context.wait_for_pause_signal_loss`` returns), the controller stops
    evaluating the condition, so the adapter pauses the robot in its place and
    resumes the same way once the signal is back. Without a release waiter (a
    context built by hand) the pause ends the execution early, as it did before
    IO pauses became resumable. A waiter that fails ends the execution with its
    error.

    Must be called with a running event loop: the cursor schedules its
    background initialization at construction time.
    """
    cursor = TrajectoryCursor(
        motion_id=context.motion_id,
        motion_group_state_stream=context.motion_group_state_stream_gen,
        joint_trajectory=context.joint_trajectory,
        # An empty list carries no action metadata; it must not be mistaken
        # for a zero-length trajectory.
        actions=list(context.combined_actions.items) or None,
        # Server-side IO overlay, attached by the cursor to every start it
        # emits (each start overrides the previously attached overlay). A
        # context that resolved path triggers carries the finished overlay.
        set_outputs=(
            context.set_outputs
            if context.set_outputs is not None
            else context.combined_actions.to_set_io()
        ),
        start_on_io=context.start_on_io,
        pause_on_io=context.pause_on_io,
        initial_location=0.0,
        detach_on_standstill=True,
        emit_motion_events=False,
    )
    # Starting immediately is move_forward policy, not a cursor capability.
    driver = _OneShotDriver(cursor, cursor.forward(), context)

    async def controller(response_stream):
        supervisor = asyncio.create_task(
            driver.run(), name=f"move_forward-supervisor-{context.motion_id}"
        )
        try:
            async for request in cursor.cntrl(response_stream):
                yield request
        finally:
            supervisor.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await supervisor
        if driver.error is not None:
            raise driver.error

    return controller


class _OneShotDriver:
    """Drives a one-shot execution to the end of the trajectory through IO pauses.

    Nobody else awaits the operation futures in one-shot execution: movement
    errors reach the protocol caller through ``cntrl`` itself, and a state
    stream that ends before the trajectory completes only resolves the future,
    matching the previous ``move_forward`` behaviour of returning once the state
    monitor is gone. Retrieving the results here also keeps asyncio from warning
    about them.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        cursor: TrajectoryCursor,
        operation: asyncio.Future[OperationResult],
        context: MovementControllerContext,
    ):
        self._cursor = cursor
        self._operation = operation
        self._wait_for_release = context.wait_for_pause_on_io_release
        self._wait_for_signal_loss = context.wait_for_pause_signal_loss
        # Set by the guard when it paused the robot because the signal source
        # went away; the drive loop then resumes through the release wait.
        self._guard_pause: asyncio.Future[OperationResult] | None = None
        self._signal_lost = False
        self._resumed = asyncio.Event()
        self.error: BaseException | None = None

    async def run(self) -> None:
        guard = (
            asyncio.create_task(self._guard(), name="move_forward-signal-guard")
            if self._wait_for_signal_loss is not None and self._wait_for_release is not None
            else None
        )
        try:
            await self._drive()
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 — surfaced to the protocol caller
            logger.error(f"move_forward cannot continue the execution: {error!r}")
            self.error = error
            self._cursor.detach()
        finally:
            if guard is not None:
                guard.cancel()
                with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await guard

    async def _drive(self) -> None:
        operation = self._operation
        while True:
            try:
                result = await operation
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                task = asyncio.current_task()
                if task is not None and task.cancelling():
                    raise  # our own cancellation (detach / teardown)
                if self._guard_pause is None:
                    return  # the operation was cancelled from outside — nothing to drive
                # The guard superseded the movement with a pause: let it settle,
                # then resume once the signal is back.
                pause, self._guard_pause = self._guard_pause, None
                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                    await pause
                result = None
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 — surfaced through cntrl
                logger.debug(f"move_forward operation ended with an error: {error!r}")
                return

            if result is not None and not result.paused_on_io and not self._signal_lost:
                return
            if self._wait_for_release is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "Movement paused on IO at location %s but no release waiter is available; "
                    "ending the execution early.",
                    result.final_location if result is not None else self._cursor.current_location,
                )
                self._cursor.detach()
                return
            logger.info(
                "Movement paused (%s) at location %s — waiting for the signal to allow motion",
                "signal source lost" if self._signal_lost else "IO condition",
                self._cursor.current_location,
            )
            await self._wait_for_release()
            logger.info("Pause signal cleared — resuming movement")
            self._signal_lost = False
            # The start re-carries pause_on_io and the IO overlay, so the pause is
            # re-armed and remaining path outputs stay attached.
            operation = self._cursor.forward()
            self._resumed.set()

    async def _guard(self) -> None:
        """Pause the robot ourselves whenever the signal's source disappears."""
        assert self._wait_for_signal_loss is not None
        while True:
            await self._wait_for_signal_loss()
            logger.warning("Pause signal source lost — pausing the movement from the SDK")
            self._signal_lost = True
            self._resumed.clear()
            pause = self._cursor.pause()  # None when nothing is moving (already paused)
            if pause is not None:
                self._guard_pause = pause
            # Re-arm only after the drive loop resumed the movement; the loss
            # waiter would otherwise return immediately while the bus is down.
            await self._resumed.wait()

STARTING = "starting"  # a start was sent, no evidence of motion since
MOVING = "moving"  # the robot moved since the last start
PAUSED_ON_IO = "paused on IO"  # the controller holds a pause_on_io pause
PAUSED_BY_APP = "paused by app"  # we paused it (signal source lost)
ENDED = "ended"  # trajectory ended at standstill

# What ``FrameTracker`` reports to the driver.
EVENT_MOVING = "moving"
EVENT_PAUSED_ON_IO = "paused_on_io"
# A resume start after which the controller showed nothing but the pause it was
# supposed to leave, for ``settle_s``: either the condition was back when the
# start arrived, or the start was not taken up. The driver tells the two apart
# by reading the signal.
EVENT_RESUME_NOT_TAKEN_UP = "resume_not_taken_up"
EVENT_PAUSED_BY_APP = "paused_by_app"
EVENT_ENDED = "ended"


class FrameTracker:
    """Interprets the execution's state frames into pause / resume / end events.

    The rules, each one a trap somebody fell into:

    * **Nothing concludes before a start.** Between initialize and start the
      controller reports ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` at standstill: a parked trajectory
      looks exactly like a paused one.
    * **Motion is only evidence.** ``RUNNING`` or ``standstill == False``. The
      mere presence of an ``execute`` block is not, it exists from initialize.
    * **End = ``Ended`` at standstill, after this execution moved.** A terminal
      frame for a motion that never happened is not a completion (that was the
      stale-frame shape of the earlier ``execute()`` wedge on this cell). Older
      controllers drop the ``execute`` block the instant the robot settles, so
      a bare standstill right after ``Ended`` frames also counts.
    * **After a resume start, repeated ``PAUSED_ON_IO`` is the old pause**
      until a different frame arrives. If none has after ``settle_s``, that is
      its own event (``EVENT_RESUME_NOT_TAKEN_UP``), not a new pause. The first
      start leaves no IO pause, so a ``PAUSED_ON_IO`` after it is a pause at
      once (the condition held at the start).
    * **``PAUSED_BY_USER`` is our own pause only if we sent one.**
    """

    def __init__(self, end_location: float, settle_s: float = RESUME_SETTLE_MS / 1000.0):
        self.end_location = end_location
        self.settle_s = settle_s
        self.phase = PARKED
        self.frames = 0
        self.name: str | None = None
        self.standstill: bool | None = None
        self.location: float | None = None
        self.trajectory_id: str | None = None
        self.min_location: float | None = None
        self.max_location: float | None = None
        self.ever_moved = False
        self.started_at: float | None = None
        self.starts = 0
        self.pause_sent = False
        self._filter_old_pause = False
        self._seen_ended = False

    @property
    def travelled(self) -> float:
        if self.min_location is None or self.max_location is None:
            return 0.0
        return self.max_location - self.min_location

    def started(self, now: float) -> None:
        """A ``StartMovementRequest`` was just sent."""
        self.starts += 1
        self.started_at = now
        self.pause_sent = False
        # Frames repeating a pause the controller is leaving must not count as
        # a new one. Only a start out of an IO pause has one to leave -- the
        # SDK's cursor applies the same rule to starts out of a paused state.
        self._filter_old_pause = self.phase == PAUSED_ON_IO
        self.phase = STARTING

    def paused_by_app(self) -> None:
        """A ``PauseMovementRequest`` was just sent."""
        self.pause_sent = True

    def frame(
        self,
        name: str | None,
        standstill: bool,
        location: float | None,
        now: float,
        trajectory_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> str | None:
        """Take one state frame; return an event when the phase changed."""
        self.frames += 1
        previous_name = self.name
        self.name, self.standstill = name, standstill
        if location is not None:
            self.location = location
        if trajectory_id is not None:
            self.trajectory_id = trajectory_id
        if self.phase in (PARKED, ENDED):
            return None

        if location is not None:
            self.min_location = (
                location if self.min_location is None else min(self.min_location, location)
            )
            self.max_location = (
                location if self.max_location is None else max(self.max_location, location)
            )

        moving = name == "Running" or (name is not None and not standstill)
        if name != "PausedOnIO" or moving:
            self._filter_old_pause = False
        if name == "Ended":
            self._seen_ended = True

        if moving:
            self.ever_moved = True
            if self.phase != MOVING and name == "Running":
                self.phase = MOVING
                return EVENT_MOVING
            return None

        if not standstill:
            return None

        if name == "Ended" and self.ever_moved:
            self.phase = ENDED
            return EVENT_ENDED
        if name is None and self.ever_moved and self._seen_ended and previous_name == "Ended":
            self.phase = ENDED
            return EVENT_ENDED
        if name == "PausedOnIO" and not self._filter_old_pause and self.phase != PAUSED_ON_IO:
            self.phase = PAUSED_ON_IO
            return EVENT_PAUSED_ON_IO
        if name == "PausedByUser" and self.pause_sent and self.phase != PAUSED_BY_APP:
            self.phase = PAUSED_BY_APP
            return EVENT_PAUSED_BY_APP
        return None

    def tick(self, now: float) -> str | None:
        """Time-based rule: nothing but the old pause for ``settle_s`` after a resume start."""
        if (
            self._filter_old_pause
            and self.phase == STARTING
            and self.name == "PausedOnIO"
            and self.standstill
            and self.started_at is not None
            and now - self.started_at >= self.settle_s
        ):
            self._filter_old_pause = False
            self.phase = PAUSED_ON_IO
            return EVENT_RESUME_NOT_TAKEN_UP
        return None

    def describe(self) -> str:
        location = "?" if self.location is None else f"{self.location:.4f}"
        return (
            f"phase={self.phase} state={self.name or 'none'} standstill={self.standstill} "
            f"loc={location}/{self.end_location:.4f} starts={self.starts} "
            f"travelled={self.travelled:.4f} frames={self.frames}"
        )
