logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunSettings:
    """One run's settings: the start arguments, gaps filled from the constants.

    Resolved once per start and passed down, rather than written back onto the
    module: the hosted app is long-lived, and one run's arguments must not
    become the next run's defaults.
    """

    loop_iterations: int
    loop_pause_s: float
    playback_speed_percent: int
    run_home: bool
    run_combined: bool
    home_every_iteration: bool
    home_profile: SpeedProfile
    outbound_profile: SpeedProfile
    return_profile: SpeedProfile
    axis_far_mm: float
    square_half_edge_mm: float
    square_blending_radius_mm: float
    square_1_direction: int
    square_2_direction: int
    square_keeps_home_config: bool
    motion: str
    linear_half_stroke_mm: float
    linear_sync_offset_s: float
    linear_direction: str
    linear_arm_profile: SpeedProfile | None


def _pick(value, default):
    return default if value is None else value


def resolve_run_settings(
    *,
    loop_iterations: int | None = None,
    loop_pause_s: float | None = None,
    playback_speed_percent: int | None = None,
    run_home: bool | None = None,
    run_combined: bool | None = None,
    home_every_iteration: bool | None = None,
    home_profile: str | None = None,
    outbound_profile: str | None = None,
    return_profile: str | None = None,
    axis_far_mm: float | None = None,
    square_edge_mm: float | None = None,
    square_blending_radius_mm: float | None = None,
    square_1_direction: int | None = None,
    square_2_direction: int | None = None,
    square_keeps_home_config: bool | None = None,
    motion: str | None = None,
    linear_stroke_mm: float | None = None,
    linear_sync_offset_s: float | None = None,
    linear_direction: str | None = None,
    linear_arm_profile: str | None = None,
) -> RunSettings:
    """Fill every unset argument from its module constant, and fence the rest.

    The constants are read here, at start time, not at import — so a ``LAB_*``
    override applied by lab_app after import is the default, as it should be.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``axis_far_mm`` lies outside home..``AXIS_FAR_MM``,
            ``square_edge_mm`` is larger than ``SQUARE_EDGE_MM``,
            ``linear_stroke_mm`` is larger than ``LINEAR_STROKE_MM``, or the
            motion / linear direction is not one of ``MOTIONS`` /
            ``LINEAR_DIRECTIONS``.
    """
    rail_min, rail_max = sorted((AXIS_HOME_MM, AXIS_FAR_MM))
    if axis_far_mm is not None and not rail_min <= axis_far_mm <= rail_max:
        raise ValueError(
            f"axis_far_mm={axis_far_mm} is outside the configured rail travel "
            f"{AXIS_HOME_MM}..{AXIS_FAR_MM} mm; only a shorter travel can be "
            f"started — extending it is an edit to AXIS_FAR_MM."
        )
    if square_edge_mm is not None and square_edge_mm > SQUARE_EDGE_MM:
        raise ValueError(
            f"square_edge_mm={square_edge_mm} is larger than the configured "
            f"SQUARE_EDGE_MM={SQUARE_EDGE_MM}; only a smaller square can be "
            f"started — growing it is an edit to SQUARE_EDGE_MM."
        )
    if linear_stroke_mm is not None and linear_stroke_mm > LINEAR_STROKE_MM:
        raise ValueError(
            f"linear_stroke_mm={linear_stroke_mm} is larger than the configured "
            f"LINEAR_STROKE_MM={LINEAR_STROKE_MM}; only a shorter stroke can be "
            f"started — lengthening it is an edit to LINEAR_STROKE_MM."
        )
    chosen_motion = _pick(motion, MOTION)
    if chosen_motion not in MOTIONS:
        raise ValueError(f"motion={chosen_motion!r} is not one of {MOTIONS}")
    chosen_direction = _pick(linear_direction, LINEAR_DIRECTION)
    if chosen_direction not in LINEAR_DIRECTIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"linear_direction={chosen_direction!r} is not one of {LINEAR_DIRECTIONS}"
        )

    def profile(name: str | None, default: SpeedProfile) -> SpeedProfile:
        return default if name is None else PROFILES[name]

    return RunSettings(
        loop_iterations=_pick(loop_iterations, LOOP_ITERATIONS),
        loop_pause_s=_pick(loop_pause_s, LOOP_PAUSE_S),
        playback_speed_percent=_pick(playback_speed_percent, PLAYBACK_SPEED_PERCENT),
        run_home=_pick(run_home, RUN_HOME),
        run_combined=_pick(run_combined, RUN_COMBINED),
        home_every_iteration=_pick(home_every_iteration, HOME_EVERY_ITERATION),
        home_profile=profile(home_profile, HOME_PROFILE),
        outbound_profile=profile(outbound_profile, OUTBOUND_PROFILE),
        return_profile=profile(return_profile, RETURN_PROFILE),
        axis_far_mm=_pick(axis_far_mm, AXIS_FAR_MM),
        # Derived per run from the argument, so unlike a LAB_SQUARE_EDGE_MM
        # override an argument cannot leave the half-edge stale.
        square_half_edge_mm=(SQUARE_HALF_EDGE_MM if square_edge_mm is None
                             else square_edge_mm / 2.0),
        square_blending_radius_mm=_pick(square_blending_radius_mm, SQUARE_BLENDING_RADIUS_MM),
        square_1_direction=_pick(square_1_direction, SQUARE_1_DIRECTION),
        square_2_direction=_pick(square_2_direction, SQUARE_2_DIRECTION),
        square_keeps_home_config=_pick(square_keeps_home_config, SQUARE_KEEPS_HOME_CONFIG),
        motion=chosen_motion,
        linear_half_stroke_mm=_pick(linear_stroke_mm, LINEAR_STROKE_MM) / 2.0,
        linear_sync_offset_s=_pick(linear_sync_offset_s, LINEAR_SYNC_OFFSET_S),
        linear_direction=chosen_direction,
        linear_arm_profile=(LINEAR_ARM_PROFILE if linear_arm_profile is None
                            else PROFILES[linear_arm_profile]),
    )


def pose_at(anchor: Pose, position: Vector3d, keep_config: bool) -> Pose:
    """``anchor``'s orientation at ``position``, optionally with its STATUS/TURN."""
    orientation = anchor.orientation
    pose = Pose((position.x, position.y, position.z,
                 orientation.x, orientation.y, orientation.z))
    if keep_config:
        pose.kinematic_configuration = anchor.kinematic_configuration
    return pose


def square_corners(anchor: Pose, direction: int, half_edge_mm: float) -> list[Vector3d]:
    """The square's path points: top-edge midpoint, four corners, back to it.

    Laid out in the world Y-Z plane around ``anchor`` + ``SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET``.
    ``direction`` +1 leaves the midpoint towards +Y; -1 mirrors it.
    """
    center = anchor.position + SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET
    h = half_edge_mm

    def at(dy: float, dz: float) -> Vector3d:
        return center + Vector3d(x=0.0, y=dy * direction, z=dz)

    start = at(0.0, h)                      # middle of the top edge
    return [start, at(h, h), at(h, -h), at(-h, -h), at(-h, h), start]


def square_actions(
    anchor: Pose, settings: MotionSettings, direction: int, run: RunSettings
) -> list:
    """A full square around ``anchor``: LIN in, four blended corners, LIN back.

    Every leg is a straight ``lin``. The four corner targets carry
    ``run.square_blending_radius_mm``; the entry and exit points on the top edge do
    not, so each lap starts and ends at an exact position. The lead-in and
    lead-out collapse to nothing when ``SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET`` already puts
    ``anchor`` on the square's outline.
    """
    blended = settings.model_copy(update={"blending_radius": run.square_blending_radius_mm})

    def corner_pose(position: Vector3d) -> Pose:
        return pose_at(anchor, position, run.square_keeps_home_config)

    points = square_corners(anchor, direction, run.square_half_edge_mm)
    start, corners, back = points[0], points[1:-1], points[-1]

    on_outline = math.dist(start.to_tuple(), anchor.position.to_tuple()) < 1e-6
    lead_in = [] if on_outline else [lin(corner_pose(start), settings=settings)]
    lead_out = [] if on_outline else [lin(anchor, settings=settings)]

    return [
        *lead_in,
        *[lin(corner_pose(corner), settings=blended) for corner in corners],
        lin(corner_pose(back), settings=settings),   # exact stop where the lap began
        *lead_out,
    ]


def carriage_direction(from_mm: float, to_mm: float) -> Vector3d:
    """World unit vector the carriage travels along when E1 goes ``from_mm`` -> ``to_mm``.

    From ir999r01's measured ``RailRobroot`` (the same calibration its arm
    mounting comes from), so the stroke is parallel to the rail as calibrated.

    Raises:
        ValueError: no calibration for ``ROBOT_ID``, or the leg does not move.
    """
    calibration = rail_robroot_for(ROBOT_ID)
    if calibration is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{ROBOT_ID} has no RAIL_ROBROOT entry: rail direction unknown")
    if to_mm == from_mm:
        raise ValueError(f"the rail does not move ({from_mm} mm): no direction to oppose")
    sign = 1.0 if to_mm > from_mm else -1.0
    dx, dy, dz = calibration.direction
    norm = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
    return Vector3d(x=sign * dx / norm, y=sign * dy / norm, z=sign * dz / norm)


def linear_stroke_poses(anchor: Pose, run: RunSettings) -> tuple[Pose, Pose]:
    """The stroke's two ends, (outbound start, outbound end), centred on ``anchor``.

    The outbound stroke runs opposite to the carriage's outbound travel, or
    along it for ``run.linear_direction == "same"``; the return leg simply
    runs it back, so it keeps the same relation to that leg's carriage travel.
    """
    carriage = carriage_direction(AXIS_HOME_MM, run.axis_far_mm)
    arm_direction = carriage if run.linear_direction == "same" else -carriage
    half = arm_direction * run.linear_half_stroke_mm
    return (pose_at(anchor, anchor.position - half, keep_config=True),
            pose_at(anchor, anchor.position + half, keep_config=True))


def _segment_speeds(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory) -> list[tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """(t_start, t_end, joint-space speed) per sample segment.

    Speed is the Euclidean norm of the joint velocity vector — the rail's own
    speed for its single joint, a combined measure for the arm's six.
    """
    times = [float(t) for t in trajectory.times]
    joints = [list(j) for j in trajectory.joint_positions]
    segments = []
    for i in range(len(times) - 1):
        dt = times[i + 1] - times[i]
        if dt <= 0.0:
            continue
        speed = math.sqrt(sum((b - a) ** 2 for a, b in zip(joints[i], joints[i + 1])))
        segments.append((times[i], times[i + 1], speed / dt))
    return segments


def deceleration_onset(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, fraction: float = 0.99) -> float:
    """When the trajectory leaves its peak speed for good — its deceleration onset.

    The end of the last segment still at ``fraction`` of the peak: the start of
    the braking ramp for a trapezoid or S-curve, the apex for a move too short
    to cruise.

    Raises:
        ValueError: the trajectory does not move.
    """
    segments = _segment_speeds(trajectory)
    peak = max((speed for _, _, speed in segments), default=0.0)
    if peak <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("trajectory does not move: no deceleration to align with")
    return max(t_end for _, t_end, speed in segments if speed >= fraction * peak)


def acceleration_end(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, fraction: float = 0.99) -> float:
    """When the trajectory first reaches ``fraction`` of its peak speed."""
    segments = _segment_speeds(trajectory)
    peak = max((speed for _, _, speed in segments), default=0.0)
    return min((t_start for t_start, _, speed in segments if speed >= fraction * peak),
               default=0.0)


def delayed(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, seconds: float) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
    """The same trajectory starting ``seconds`` later.

    Only the times move; ``combine_on_shared_clock`` holds a group at its first
    sample until its own first time, so the delayed group simply waits.
    """
    return trajectory.model_copy(
        update={"times": [float(t) + seconds for t in trajectory.times]}
    )


async def run_linear_leg(
    motion_group, linear, *, tcp, arm_setup, target_mm: float, arm_target: Pose,
    rail_profile: SpeedProfile, arm_profile: SpeedProfile, run: RunSettings,
) -> None:
    """One leg of the linear counter-motion: rail to ``target_mm``, arm stroke timed onto it.

    Both motions are planned first, the arm's start is placed at the rail's
    deceleration onset plus ``run.linear_sync_offset_s``, and the two are run
    as one synchronized trajectory. Planning is from the live joints, so the
    arm must already stand at the stroke's other end.
    """
    rail_trajectory = await plan_with_watchdog(
        linear, [jnt((target_mm,), settings=rail_profile.rail)], RAIL_TCP
    )
    arm_trajectory = await plan_with_watchdog(
        motion_group, [lin(arm_target, settings=arm_profile.arm)], tcp,
        motion_group_setup=arm_setup,
    )

    rail_end = float(rail_trajectory.times[-1])
    decel_onset = deceleration_onset(rail_trajectory)
    arm_start = decel_onset + run.linear_sync_offset_s
    arm_accel = acceleration_end(arm_trajectory)
    arm_duration = float(arm_trajectory.times[-1])

    # A negative start would put the arm ahead of the rail's own t=0: delay the
    # rail instead, so the earliest group still starts the shared clock.
    rail_shift = max(0.0, -arm_start)
    arm_shift = max(0.0, arm_start)
    overlap = max(0.0, min(rail_end, arm_start + arm_accel) - max(decel_onset, arm_start))
    logger.info(
        "timing (planned s, before playback scaling): rail decelerates %.3f-%.3f; "
        "arm starts %.3f, accelerates until %.3f, ends %.3f; overlap %.3f s",
        decel_onset + rail_shift, rail_end + rail_shift,
        arm_start + rail_shift, arm_start + rail_shift + arm_accel,
        arm_start + rail_shift + arm_duration, overlap,
    )

    combined = combine_on_shared_clock({
        motion_group.id: delayed(arm_trajectory, arm_shift),
        linear.id: delayed(rail_trajectory, rail_shift),
    })
    await execute_planned_multi(
        motion_group, linear, combined,
        tcp=tcp, playback_speed_in_percent=run.playback_speed_percent,
    )


async def move_rail(
    linear, target_mm: float, profile: SpeedProfile, *, playback_speed_percent: int
) -> None:
    """Move the rail to ``target_mm``. Joint motion; the arm is not involved."""
    logger.info("Rail -> %.1f mm at %s", target_mm, profile.describe())
    await plan_and_execute_with_playback_speed(
        linear,
        [jnt((target_mm,), settings=profile.rail)],
        tcp=RAIL_TCP,
        playback_speed_in_percent=playback_speed_percent,
    )
    logger.info("Rail at %.1f mm", target_mm)


async def move_arm(
    motion_group, linear, actions: list, *, tcp, playback_speed_percent: int
) -> None:
    """Run an arm block, planned at ``AXIS_MOUNTING_MM`` wherever the rail is."""
    await plan_and_execute_at_axis(
        motion_group, linear, actions,
        tcp=tcp, axis_mm=AXIS_MOUNTING_MM,
        playback_speed_in_percent=playback_speed_percent, robot_id=ROBOT_ID,
    )


async def move_arm_and_rail(
    motion_group, linear, actions: list, *, tcp, target_mm: float, profile: SpeedProfile,
    playback_speed_percent: int,
) -> None:
    """Run the arm block and the rail move at the same time.

    Deliberately not ``move_synced``: that helper re-plans the arm against the
    mounting for the rail's destination, and here the arm's frame does not
    follow the carriage. If either side fails the other is cancelled, so a
    failed plan never leaves a motion group travelling unsupervised.
    """
    tasks = (
        asyncio.create_task(
            move_arm(motion_group, linear, actions, tcp=tcp,
                     playback_speed_percent=playback_speed_percent),
            name="probe-arm",
        ),
        asyncio.create_task(
            move_rail(linear, target_mm, profile,
                      playback_speed_percent=playback_speed_percent),
            name="probe-rail",
        ),
    )
    try:
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    except BaseException:
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        raise


def _report_durations(durations: list[float]) -> None:
    """Log how long each pass took, and how much they varied."""
    if not durations:
        return
    logger.info(
        "combined loop: %d iteration(s), %.2f s min / %.2f s mean / %.2f s max "
        "(spread %.2f s)",
        len(durations), min(durations), sum(durations) / len(durations),
        max(durations), max(durations) - min(durations),
    )
    for index, elapsed in enumerate(durations, start=1):
        logger.info("  iteration %3d: %.2f s", index, elapsed)

                    "own limits. Empty: LINEAR_ARM_PROFILE, else the leg's profile.")] = None,
):
    """Repeat combined.py's two legs until stopped, timing every pass.

    Every argument is optional; an empty one means the deployment's value.
    """

    run = resolve_run_settings(
        loop_iterations=loop_iterations,
        loop_pause_s=loop_pause_s,
        playback_speed_percent=playback_speed_percent,
        run_home=run_home,
        run_combined=run_combined,
        home_every_iteration=home_every_iteration,
        home_profile=home_profile,
        outbound_profile=outbound_profile,
        return_profile=return_profile,
        axis_far_mm=axis_far_mm,
        square_edge_mm=square_edge_mm,
        square_blending_radius_mm=square_blending_radius_mm,
        square_1_direction=square_1_direction,
        square_2_direction=square_2_direction,
        square_keeps_home_config=square_keeps_home_config,
        motion=motion,
        linear_stroke_mm=linear_stroke_mm,
        linear_sync_offset_s=linear_sync_offset_s,
        linear_direction=linear_direction,
        linear_arm_profile=linear_arm_profile,
    )
    # Before anything moves: a linear run with no rail travel or no calibration
    # should fail here, not after homing.
    stroke = linear_stroke_poses(HOME_POSE, run) if run.motion == "linear" else None

    logger.info("Initializing combined-loop probe...")
    logger.info("run settings: %s", run)

    cell = ctx.nova.cell(CELL_ID)
    controller = await resolve_controller(cell, ROBOT_ID, *CONTROLLER_ALIASES)
    motion_group = controller[0]   # 6-axis arm
    linear = controller[1]         # external linear axis (rail), 1-DOF

    tcp = await resolve_motion_group_tcp(motion_group, TCP_NAME)
    await set_default_mode_control(controller)

    logger.info("Combined-loop probe initialized.")

    async def home() -> None:
        logger.info("Homing: arm -> P0, rail -> %.1f mm", AXIS_HOME_MM)
        await move_arm_and_rail(
            motion_group, linear, [ptp(HOME_POSE, settings=run.home_profile.arm)],
            tcp=tcp, target_mm=AXIS_HOME_MM, profile=run.home_profile,
            playback_speed_percent=run.playback_speed_percent,
        )
        logger.info("At home")

    if run.run_home:
        await home()

    if not run.run_combined:
        logger.info("run_combined is off — nothing to loop.")
        return

    legs = (
        (run.axis_far_mm, run.square_1_direction, run.outbound_profile),
        (AXIS_HOME_MM, run.square_2_direction, run.return_profile),
    )

    arm_setup = None
    at_stroke_start = False
    if stroke is not None:
        # The arm is planned at AXIS_MOUNTING_MM throughout (see move_arm);
        # the linear legs plan it directly, so they need the same setup.
        arm_setup = await axis_mounting_setup(
            motion_group, linear, tcp, AXIS_MOUNTING_MM, ROBOT_ID
        )

    async def stroke_lead(target: Pose, what: str) -> None:
        logger.info("linear: arm %s at %s", what, run.home_profile.describe())
        await move_arm(motion_group, linear, [lin(target, settings=run.home_profile.arm)],
                       tcp=tcp, playback_speed_percent=run.playback_speed_percent)

    durations: list[float] = []
    completed = 0
    try:
        while run.loop_iterations == 0 or completed < run.loop_iterations:
            logger.info("=== iteration %d ===", completed + 1)
            if run.run_home and run.home_every_iteration and completed:
                await home()
                at_stroke_start = False
            if stroke is not None and not at_stroke_start:
                await stroke_lead(stroke[0], "to the stroke start")
                at_stroke_start = True

            started = time.monotonic()
            for leg_index, (target_mm, direction, profile) in enumerate(legs):
                leg_started = time.monotonic()
                if stroke is None:
                    logger.info(
                        "square direction %+d while the rail travels to %.1f mm, at %s",
                        direction, target_mm, profile.name,
                    )
                    await move_arm_and_rail(
                        motion_group, linear,
                        square_actions(HOME_POSE, profile.arm, direction, run),
                        tcp=tcp, target_mm=target_mm, profile=profile,
                        playback_speed_percent=run.playback_speed_percent,
                    )
                else:
                    arm_profile = run.linear_arm_profile or profile
                    arm_target = stroke[1] if leg_index == 0 else stroke[0]
                    logger.info(
                        "linear stroke %s the rail travelling to %.1f mm; "
                        "rail at %s, arm at %s",
                        "with" if run.linear_direction == "same" else "against",
                        target_mm, profile.describe(), arm_profile.describe(),
                    )
                    await run_linear_leg(
                        motion_group, linear, tcp=tcp, arm_setup=arm_setup,
                        target_mm=target_mm, arm_target=arm_target,
                        rail_profile=profile, arm_profile=arm_profile, run=run,
                    )
                logger.info("leg done in %.2f s", time.monotonic() - leg_started)

            elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
            durations.append(elapsed)
            completed += 1
            logger.info("iteration %d done in %.2f s: arm %s, rail at home", completed,
                        elapsed, "at P0" if stroke is None else "at the stroke start")

            if run.loop_iterations and completed >= run.loop_iterations:
                break
            logger.info(
                "pausing %.1f s. Ctrl+C NOW to stop cleanly; an interrupt "
                "mid-leg aborts the motion.", run.loop_pause_s,
            )
            await asyncio.sleep(run.loop_pause_s)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logger.info("Interrupted after %d complete iteration(s).", completed)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # Hosted as a NOVA program, a stop arrives as cancellation. Report, then
        # re-raise: swallowing it would leave the caller believing the loop ran
        # to completion, and novax would record a stopped program as finished.
        logger.info("Stopped after %d complete iteration(s).", completed)
        raise
    finally:
        # In a finally: a failed plan or a watchdog stops the loop by raising,
        # and the timings up to that point are most of what the run was for.
        _report_durations(durations)

    if stroke is not None and at_stroke_start:
        await stroke_lead(HOME_POSE, "back to P0")
    logger.info("Combined-loop probe finished after %d iteration(s).", completed)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_program(main)

449	def pose_at(anchor: Pose, position: Vector3d, keep_config: bool) -> Pose:
450	    """``anchor``'s orientation at ``position``, optionally with its STATUS/TURN."""
451	    orientation = anchor.orientation
452	    pose = Pose((position.x, position.y, position.z,
453	                 orientation.x, orientation.y, orientation.z))
454	    if keep_config:
455	        pose.kinematic_configuration = anchor.kinematic_configuration
456	    return pose

459	def square_corners(anchor: Pose, direction: int, half_edge_mm: float) -> list[Vector3d]:
460	    """The square's path points: top-edge midpoint, four corners, back to it.
461	
462	    Laid out in the world Y-Z plane around ``anchor`` + ``SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET``.
463	    ``direction`` +1 leaves the midpoint towards +Y; -1 mirrors it.
464	    """
465	    center = anchor.position + SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET
466	    h = half_edge_mm
467	
468	    def at(dy: float, dz: float) -> Vector3d:
469	        return center + Vector3d(x=0.0, y=dy * direction, z=dz)
470	
471	    start = at(0.0, h)                      # middle of the top edge
472	    return [start, at(h, h), at(h, -h), at(-h, -h), at(-h, h), start]
473	
474	
475	def square_actions(
476	    anchor: Pose, settings: MotionSettings, direction: int, run: RunSettings
477	) -> list:
478	    """A full square around ``anchor``: LIN in, four blended corners, LIN back.
479	
480	    Every leg is a straight ``lin``. The four corner targets carry
481	    ``run.square_blending_radius_mm``; the entry and exit points on the top edge do
482	    not, so each lap starts and ends at an exact position. The lead-in and
483	    lead-out collapse to nothing when ``SQUARE_CENTER_OFFSET`` already puts
484	    ``anchor`` on the square's outline.
485	    """
486	    blended = settings.model_copy(update={"blending_radius": run.square_blending_radius_mm})
487	
488	    def corner_pose(position: Vector3d) -> Pose:
489	        return pose_at(anchor, position, run.square_keeps_home_config)
490	
491	    points = square_corners(anchor, direction, run.square_half_edge_mm)
492	    start, corners, back = points[0], points[1:-1], points[-1]
493	
494	    on_outline = math.dist(start.to_tuple(), anchor.position.to_tuple()) < 1e-6
495	    lead_in = [] if on_outline else [lin(corner_pose(start), settings=settings)]
496	    lead_out = [] if on_outline else [lin(anchor, settings=settings)]
497	
498	    return [
499	        *lead_in,
500	        *[lin(corner_pose(corner), settings=blended) for corner in corners],
501	        lin(corner_pose(back), settings=settings),   # exact stop where the lap began
502	        *lead_out,
503	    ]

506	def carriage_direction(from_mm: float, to_mm: float) -> Vector3d:
507	    """World unit vector the carriage travels along when E1 goes ``from_mm`` -> ``to_mm``.
508	
509	    From ir999r01's measured ``RailRobroot`` (the same calibration its arm
510	    mounting comes from), so the stroke is parallel to the rail as calibrated.
511	
512	    Raises:
513	        ValueError: no calibration for ``ROBOT_ID``, or the leg does not move.
514	    """
515	    calibration = rail_robroot_for(ROBOT_ID)
516	    if calibration is None:
517	        raise ValueError(f"{ROBOT_ID} has no RAIL_ROBROOT entry: rail direction unknown")
518	    if to_mm == from_mm:
519	        raise ValueError(f"the rail does not move ({from_mm} mm): no direction to oppose")
520	    sign = 1.0 if to_mm > from_mm else -1.0
521	    dx, dy, dz = calibration.direction
522	    norm = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
523	    return Vector3d(x=sign * dx / norm, y=sign * dy / norm, z=sign * dz / norm)
524

526	def linear_stroke_poses(anchor: Pose, run: RunSettings) -> tuple[Pose, Pose]:
527	    """The stroke's two ends, (outbound start, outbound end), centred on ``anchor``.
528	
529	    The outbound stroke runs opposite to the carriage's outbound travel, or
530	    along it for ``run.linear_direction == "same"``; the return leg simply
531	    runs it back, so it keeps the same relation to that leg's carriage travel.
532	    """
533	    carriage = carriage_direction(AXIS_HOME_MM, run.axis_far_mm)
534	    arm_direction = carriage if run.linear_direction == "same" else -carriage
535	    half = arm_direction * run.linear_half_stroke_mm
536	    return (pose_at(anchor, anchor.position - half, keep_config=True),
537	            pose_at(anchor, anchor.position + half, keep_config=True))

539	
540	def _segment_speeds(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory) -> list[tuple[float, float, float]]:
541	    """(t_start, t_end, joint-space speed) per sample segment.
542	
543	    Speed is the Euclidean norm of the joint velocity vector — the rail's own
544	    speed for its single joint, a combined measure for the arm's six.
545	    """
546	    times = [float(t) for t in trajectory.times]
547	    joints = [list(j) for j in trajectory.joint_positions]
548	    segments = []
549	    for i in range(len(times) - 1):
550	        dt = times[i + 1] - times[i]
551	        if dt <= 0.0:
552	            continue
553	        speed = math.sqrt(sum((b - a) ** 2 for a, b in zip(joints[i], joints[i + 1])))
554	        segments.append((times[i], times[i + 1], speed / dt))
555	    return segments
556	
557	
558	def deceleration_onset(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, fraction: float = 0.99) -> float:
559	    """When the trajectory leaves its peak speed for good — its deceleration onset.
560	
561	    The end of the last segment still at ``fraction`` of the peak: the start of
562	    the braking ramp for a trapezoid or S-curve, the apex for a move too short
563	    to cruise.
564	
565	    Raises:
566	        ValueError: the trajectory does not move.
567	    """
568	    segments = _segment_speeds(trajectory)
569	    peak = max((speed for _, _, speed in segments), default=0.0)
570	    if peak <= 0.0:
571	        raise ValueError("trajectory does not move: no deceleration to align with")
572	    return max(t_end for _, t_end, speed in segments if speed >= fraction * peak)
573	
574	
575	def acceleration_end(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, fraction: float = 0.99) -> float:
576	    """When the trajectory first reaches ``fraction`` of its peak speed."""
577	    segments = _segment_speeds(trajectory)
578	    peak = max((speed for _, _, speed in segments), default=0.0)
579	    return min((t_start for t_start, _, speed in segments if speed >= fraction * peak),
580	               default=0.0)
581	
582	
583	def delayed(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory, seconds: float) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
584	    """The same trajectory starting ``seconds`` later.
585	
586	    Only the times move; ``combine_on_shared_clock`` holds a group at its first
587	    sample until its own first time, so the delayed group simply waits.
588	    """
589	    return trajectory.model_copy(
590	        update={"times": [float(t) + seconds for t in trajectory.times]}
591	    )

594	async def run_linear_leg(
595	    motion_group, linear, *, tcp, arm_setup, target_mm: float, arm_target: Pose,
596	    rail_profile: SpeedProfile, arm_profile: SpeedProfile, run: RunSettings,
597	) -> None:
598	    """One leg of the linear counter-motion: rail to ``target_mm``, arm stroke timed onto it.
599	
600	    Both motions are planned first, the arm's start is placed at the rail's
601	    deceleration onset plus ``run.linear_sync_offset_s``, and the two are run
602	    as one synchronized trajectory. Planning is from the live joints, so the
603	    arm must already stand at the stroke's other end.
604	    """
605	    rail_trajectory = await plan_with_watchdog(
606	        linear, [jnt((target_mm,), settings=rail_profile.rail)], RAIL_TCP
607	    )
608	    arm_trajectory = await plan_with_watchdog(
609	        motion_group, [lin(arm_target, settings=arm_profile.arm)], tcp,
610	        motion_group_setup=arm_setup,
611	    )
612	
613	    rail_end = float(rail_trajectory.times[-1])
614	    decel_onset = deceleration_onset(rail_trajectory)
615	    arm_start = decel_onset + run.linear_sync_offset_s
616	    arm_accel = acceleration_end(arm_trajectory)
617	    arm_duration = float(arm_trajectory.times[-1])
618	
619	    # A negative start would put the arm ahead of the rail's own t=0: delay the
620	    # rail instead, so the earliest group still starts the shared clock.
621	    rail_shift = max(0.0, -arm_start)
622	    arm_shift = max(0.0, arm_start)
623	    overlap = max(0.0, min(rail_end, arm_start + arm_accel) - max(decel_onset, arm_start))
624	    logger.info(
625	        "timing (planned s, before playback scaling): rail decelerates %.3f-%.3f; "
626	        "arm starts %.3f, accelerates until %.3f, ends %.3f; overlap %.3f s",
627	        decel_onset + rail_shift, rail_end + rail_shift,
628	        arm_start + rail_shift, arm_start + rail_shift + arm_accel,
629	        arm_start + rail_shift + arm_duration, overlap,
630	    )
631	
632	    combined = combine_on_shared_clock({
633	        motion_group.id: delayed(arm_trajectory, arm_shift),
634	        linear.id: delayed(rail_trajectory, rail_shift),
635	    })
636	    await execute_planned_multi(
637	        motion_group, linear, combined,
638	        tcp=tcp, playback_speed_in_percent=run.playback_speed_percent,
639	    )

667	async def move_arm_and_rail(
668	    motion_group, linear, actions: list, *, tcp, target_mm: float, profile: SpeedProfile,
669	    playback_speed_percent: int,
670	) -> None:
671	    """Run the arm block and the rail move at the same time.
672	
673	    Deliberately not ``move_synced``: that helper re-plans the arm against the
674	    mounting for the rail's destination, and here the arm's frame does not
675	    follow the carriage. If either side fails the other is cancelled, so a
676	    failed plan never leaves a motion group travelling unsupervised.
677	    """
678	    tasks = (
679	        asyncio.create_task(
680	            move_arm(motion_group, linear, actions, tcp=tcp,
681	                     playback_speed_percent=playback_speed_percent),
682	            name="probe-arm",
683	        ),
684	        asyncio.create_task(
685	            move_rail(linear, target_mm, profile,
686	                      playback_speed_percent=playback_speed_percent),
687	            name="probe-rail",
688	        ),
689	    )
690	    try:
691	        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
692	    except BaseException:
693	        for task in tasks:
694	            task.cancel()
695	        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
696	        raise

content.text:
It isn't standstill being detected too early at the end of the leg. The rail's operation was reported finished before it had even started, and your log shows it:

```
'1@ir999r01': OperationResult(... start_location=0.0, final_location=0.0, ...)
```

That's the rail, finishing at location **0.0** on the outbound leg. The arm finished at 1.96.

**What most likely happened** (worked out from the log and the code; I haven't reproduced it):

1. **Before the controller took up the start,** the rail's state machine was in `armed`. The estimator decided that the rail was moving while it was actually parked. The only way it switches straight away is with evidence, and on the rail the joint evidence is almost certainly what fired. `joint_epsilon=1e-3` is compared per joint in the joint's own unit: 1e-3 rad is a real move for the arm, but for the prismatic rail it is **1 µm**. Encoder noise, or residual settling on a real rail, is larger than that, so the joint evidence counts as motion immediately. That bypasses the 3-frame vote that should have absorbed the flicker. This is my design mistake.
2. **Two standstill frames later** the machine concluded `paused(USER)`, which is the same chain as the original crash.
3. **The trajectory executor doesn't run in one-shot mode,** so a pause completes the operation as a normal "paused" result without any error. The rail's `forward()` future therefore resolved at 0.0.
4. **Then `RUNNING` arrived.** Robust mode logged the warning you see and went back to tracking the motion, but the operation had already been handed back, so nothing waited for the rail's own end anymore.
5. **The ensemble's `forward()` returned when the arm's end was confirmed.** The rail was still settling at that point: −3349.86 mm, and a moment later −3349.999. The next leg's initialize checks the start position and rejects it.

**Why only above about 85 %:** a faster rail has a larger following error and takes longer to settle. At lower speeds the rail had already settled by the time the arm's end was confirmed, so the missing wait on the rail didn't show. The false pause probably happens at every speed.

With the old branch, this sequence would have raised `UnexpectedTrajectoryState` in step 4. The new branch follows the controller as intended, but it doesn't reopen the operation it already completed. That's the second flaw.

**Immediate workaround, no code change:** add `NOVA_STANDSTILL_JOINT_EPSILON=none` to `lab_app/k8s` next to `LOG_LEVEL`. Setting `LOG_LEVEL=debug` as well would confirm the cause: before the failing leg you would see a frame line with `evidence=joints` on the rail group, followed by `armed → paused`.

**Fixes I'd make in the SDK:**
1. **Separate thresholds for revolute and prismatic joints,** for example 1e-3 rad and 0.1 mm. As an alternative, measured joints would only block a rest vote and never prove motion on their own.
2. **In `armed`, the commanded location decides whether the robot has moved.** A `PAUSED_BY_USER` frame at the location the start was issued from can't be a real pause after motion. The controller hasn't commanded any progress for this start, so the frame is still the parked shape. This addresses the original crash directly, independent of the flag.
3. **When following a contradiction,** if the operation was already completed from a pause this cursor never requested, log it prominently. Better, make sure the executor doesn't count such an operation as finished.

Should I implement 1 and 2, with a test that replays this rail sequence, and push them to `lab/robust-standstill`?

content.text:
In `lab_app/k8s/app.yaml` it goes in the same `env:` list as `LOG_LEVEL`, with the same indentation:

```yaml
    - name: LOG_LEVEL
      value: "debug"
    - name: NOVA_STANDSTILL_JOINT_EPSILON
      value: "none"
```

Keep the quotes: Kubernetes only accepts strings as env values, and YAML would otherwise read `none` or a bare number as another type.

I changed `LOG_LEVEL` from `"info"` to `"debug"` here too, so the log shows the per-frame `evidence=`/`jitter=` lines if something still goes wrong.

content.text:
The snippet shows correct behaviour, but it doesn't cover the part where the bug would show. It's the end of the program's last move, the arm going back to P0, and that single-arm move was never affected.

**What it does show:**
- The robot is still settling: `standstill=False` while the state is already `TrajectoryEnded`, so the machine stays in `ending`.
- The first `standstill=True` frame is still `at_rest=False`, and the machine keeps waiting.
- The second one turns `at_rest=True`, and the machine moves `ending → ended`. That's the 2-frame rest vote working as intended; with frames 4 ms apart it costs 4 ms.
- The operation finishes at 1.0, the cursor detaches, and the program ends `COMPLETED`.

**What it doesn't show** is the synchronized linear legs, where the rail was concluded at 0.0. Rather than a longer log, these lines from the same run would settle it:

```
grep -E "synchronized execution finished|following the controller|flickered|armed → paused|evidence=" <log>
```

What each result means:
- **`synchronized execution finished`:** both groups should report the same `final_location`, e.g. `1.96`. A `final_location=0.0` for `1@ir999r01` is the old bug.
- **`following the controller` or `armed → paused`:** no lines expected. Any hit means the false pause is still happening through another path.
- **`flickered`** (the INFO line `Ignored standstill flag flickered …`): each hit is a flicker the estimator absorbed. That's fine, and the count tells us how often the flag jitters.
- **`evidence=joints`:** should not appear now that joint evidence is off. `evidence=location` right at a leg start is a real motion start.

It also matters that the run went above about 85 % playback and did several iterations. That's where it failed before, and this run finished after 1 iteration.

Most of this log is python-statemachine's own DEBUG output. To keep only the SDK lines, the lab app can raise that logger in its startup code: `logging.getLogger("statemachine").setLevel(logging.INFO)`.

My earlier offer still stands: per-unit joint thresholds, and in `armed` letting the commanded location decide whether the robot has moved, so the fix doesn't rely on the environment variable.

content.text:
I pulled the log from pod `app-ir999r01-lab-79d9d7cbd5-dwjbk`, namespace `cell`. This run is clean, and it ran at the settings that failed before.

- **Settings:** 100 % playback, `maximum` profile, 1 iteration. The pod's policy line confirms `joint_epsilon=None`, so the `NOVA_STANDSTILL_JOINT_EPSILON` change took effect.
- **Both synchronized legs:** arm and rail each finished at `final_location=1.96`. Before, the rail had reported 0.0.
- **Leg starts:** every group went `armed → executing` on the `RUNNING` frame. There was no `armed → paused` and no "following the controller" warning.
- **End of the outbound leg:** the log interleaves the two groups, and the machine waited correctly for each.
  - The arm stops at 1.724 and holds its last pose, so from about location 1.85 its frames show `standstill=True` while the shared location keeps counting. It went `executing → ended` on the first `Ended` frame, which is correct because it really was standing still.
  - The rail was still braking: it showed `Ended` with `standstill=False` for several frames and stayed in `ending` until it settled. The leg was reported finished only after that.
  - This is exactly the wait that was missing in the failing run.

content.text:
This run is complete and clean. The streamed log covers the whole program, from start at 14:55:35 to `COMPLETED` at 14:57:55. Settings were 20 iterations at 100 % playback on the `robust` policy, with joint evidence off.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Iterations / synchronized legs | 20 / 40, all completed |
| `final_location` per group | 80 × `1.96`: arm and rail concluded at the end on every leg |
| `armed → paused`, "following the controller", ignored resumes | 0 |
| `ERROR` / `WARNING` / `InitMovementFailed` / `UnexpectedTrajectoryState` | 0 |
| Iteration time | 5.78–5.95 s, mean 5.92 s |

About the fastest iteration: iteration 12 took 5.78 s because its outbound leg took 2.85 s instead of about 2.93 s. Both legs planned identically, so the difference is most likely planning time, which the leg time includes, not an early conclusion.

**What the debounced standstill decision did differently from the raw flag** (about 50,700 frames):
- **Braking, 43 frames:** the raw flag said standstill while the decision was still "moving", in `ending`. That's the one-frame wait for the second rest vote at the end of each leg and lead-in move, and costs about 4 ms each time.
- **Arm holding its end pose, 40 frames:** the same one-frame lag in `executing`, while the arm stands at its last sample and waits for the rail. It's harmless because the machine only concludes on `Ended`.
- **One real flicker, at 14:55:37:** at the end of the first lead-in move, the flag showed standstill for a single frame while the robot was still braking. The old logic would have concluded "ended" there with the robot still moving, which is the early-conclusion case you suspected. The debouncing ignored it.
- **The original crash trigger never happened:** not once did the flag drop to "moving" while the robot was at rest. So this run doesn't exercise the case that failed yesterday.

**What this proves and what it doesn't:**
- The robust policy runs 40 synchronized legs at full speed with correct results and costs about 4 ms per stop.
- The false `armed → paused` from the first failure hasn't recurred with joint evidence off. That fits the explanation that 1e-3 was too tight for the rail's mm scale, but the flicker that triggered it didn't occur in this run either, so it's no proof.

**Next step:** the SDK fix, so the environment variable isn't needed:
- separate joint thresholds for revolute (rad) and prismatic (mm) axes;
- in `armed`, the commanded location decides whether the robot has moved;
- a unit test that replays the rail sequence from the failed run.

That makes the leg-start case safe by construction, whether or not a flicker shows up on the cell. Should I implement it on `lab/robust-standstill`?

class JointTypeEnum(Enum):
    REVOLUTE_JOINT = "REVOLUTE_JOINT"
    PRISMATIC_JOINT = "PRISMATIC_JOINT"


class DHParameter(BaseModel):
    """
    A single set of DH parameters.
    """

    alpha: float | None = None
    """
    Angle about x-axis in [rad].
    """
    theta: float | None = None
    """
    Angle about z-axis in [rad].
    """
    a: float | None = None
    """
    Offset along x-axis in [mm].
    """
    d: float | None = None
    """
    Offset along z-axis in [mm].
    """
    reverse_rotation_direction: bool | None = None
    """

"""Standstill estimation on top of the controller's ``standstill`` flag.

``MotionGroupState.standstill`` is an *observed* property ("NOVA treats measured
joint velocities as 0"): a threshold on measured velocities. That threshold is
currently unreliable — the flag drops to ``false`` for single frames while the
robot is at rest — and every rule of :class:`TrajectoryExecutionMachine` that reads
it can then conclude too early or see motion that never happened (a flicker in
``armed`` concluded a user pause before the start was taken up and failed the
execution when ``RUNNING`` followed).

:class:`StandstillEstimator` turns the raw flag into a debounced decision,
``at_rest``, from three inputs:

* the raw flag itself, as consecutive votes (``motion_votes`` / ``rest_votes``);
* the **commanded** trajectory location (``execute.details.location``): it only
  advances while the controller executes a command, so a change between two
  frames of the same trajectory corroborates a ``standstill=false`` frame. It
  says nothing about a ``standstill=true`` frame: the first frame at the end of
  a trajectory has a new location and a settled robot;
* the **measured** joint positions (top-level ``joint_position``): a change above
  ``joint_epsilon`` between two frames corroborates ``standstill=false`` and
  vetoes a rest vote — measured joints that moved are not at rest.

Corroborated motion switches immediately; an uncorroborated ``standstill=false``
must repeat ``motion_votes`` times. Rest needs ``rest_votes`` consecutive standstill
frames whose measured joints did not move. :meth:`StandstillConfig.passthrough` (one vote each,
no corroboration) makes ``at_rest`` equal the raw flag on the same frame — the
behaviour before this estimator existed, for when upstream fixes the flag.

A *jitter* is a run of raw flags that contradicted the decision and ended before
it could change it. Each one is reported on the reading (``jitter``) so it can be
logged — or, with :attr:`StandstillConfig.strict`, fail the execution.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

from nova import api

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StandstillConfig:
    """Tuning of :class:`StandstillEstimator`.

    Attributes:
        motion_votes: Consecutive raw ``standstill=false`` frames that prove motion
            without corroboration. ``1`` trusts a single frame.
        rest_votes: Consecutive raw ``standstill=true`` frames (without motion
            evidence) that prove rest. ``1`` trusts a single frame.
        location_epsilon: Change of the commanded trajectory location between two
            frames of the same trajectory that proves motion; ``None`` disables it.
        joint_epsilon: Largest change of any measured joint between two frames
            (rad for revolute, mm for prismatic joints) that still counts as rest;
            a larger change proves motion. ``None`` disables it.
        strict: A detected jitter fails the execution instead of being logged.
    """

    motion_votes: int = 1
    rest_votes: int = 1
    location_epsilon: float | None = None
    joint_epsilon: float | None = None
    strict: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.motion_votes < 1 or self.rest_votes < 1:
            raise ValueError("motion_votes and rest_votes must be at least 1")

    @classmethod
    def passthrough(cls) -> StandstillConfig:
        """``at_rest`` is the raw flag, on the same frame: no latency, no filtering."""
        return cls()

    @classmethod
    def robust(cls) -> StandstillConfig:
        """Debounced defaults for controllers whose flag flickers at rest."""
        return cls(motion_votes=3, rest_votes=2, location_epsilon=1e-6, joint_epsilon=1e-3)

    @property
    def is_passthrough(self) -> bool:
        return (
            self.motion_votes == 1
            and self.rest_votes == 1
            and self.location_epsilon is None
            and self.joint_epsilon is None
        )

    def with_strict(self, strict: bool) -> StandstillConfig:
        return replace(self, strict=strict)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StandstillReading:
    """The estimator's view of one frame.

    Attributes:
        raw: The frame's ``standstill`` flag.
        at_rest: The debounced decision after this frame.
        evidence: What corroborated the frame as motion (``"location"``,
            ``"joints"``), or ``None`` when only the raw flag spoke.
        jitter: This frame ended a run of raw flags that contradicted the
            decision without changing it (``"motion"``: a ``standstill=false``
            run at rest, ``"rest"``: a ``standstill=true`` run while moving).
    """

    raw: bool
    at_rest: bool
    evidence: str | None = None
    jitter: str | None = None

    @property
    def disagrees(self) -> bool:
        return self.raw != self.at_rest


def _trajectory_details(state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> api.models.TrajectoryDetails | None:
    if state.execute is not None and isinstance(
        state.execute.details, api.models.TrajectoryDetails
    ):
        return state.execute.details
    return None


def _joints(state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> list[float] | None:
    joints = state.joint_position
    # ``Joints`` is a RootModel over a list; tests may hand in plain lists.
    values = getattr(joints, "root", joints)
    return list(values) if values is not None else None


class StandstillEstimator:
    """Debounces ``standstill`` with commanded-location and measured-joint evidence.

    Pure and synchronous: feed every frame of one motion group, in order, to
    :meth:`update`. One estimator follows the robot, not an operation, so it keeps
    its decision across starts and pauses.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: StandstillConfig | None = None) -> None:
        self.config = config or StandstillConfig.passthrough()
        self.at_rest: bool | None = None
        self._motion_streak = 0
        self._rest_streak = 0
        self._last_location: tuple[str, float] | None = None
        self._last_joints: list[float] | None = None

    def update(self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> StandstillReading:
        config = self.config
        raw = state.standstill
        location_moved, joints_moved = self._evidence(state)
        # A standstill frame whose measured joints moved is not a rest vote.
        motion_frame = not raw or joints_moved
        evidence: str | None = None
        if motion_frame and joints_moved:
            evidence = "joints"
        elif motion_frame and location_moved:
            evidence = "location"

        if self.at_rest is None:
            # First frame: nothing to debounce against.
            self.at_rest = not motion_frame
            self._motion_streak = int(motion_frame)
            self._rest_streak = int(not motion_frame)
            return StandstillReading(raw=raw, at_rest=self.at_rest, evidence=evidence)

        jitter: str | None = None
        if motion_frame:
            if self._rest_streak and not self.at_rest:
                jitter = "rest"
            self._rest_streak = 0
            self._motion_streak += 1
        else:
            if self._motion_streak and self.at_rest:
                jitter = "motion"
            self._motion_streak = 0
            self._rest_streak += 1

        if self.at_rest:
            if motion_frame and (
                evidence is not None or self._motion_streak >= config.motion_votes
            ):
                self.at_rest = False
        elif self._rest_streak >= config.rest_votes:
            self.at_rest = True

        return StandstillReading(raw=raw, at_rest=self.at_rest, evidence=evidence, jitter=jitter)

    def _evidence(self, state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
        """(commanded location moved, measured joints moved) since the previous frame."""
        config = self.config
        location_moved = False
        joints_moved = False

        details = _trajectory_details(state)
        if details is not None:
            location = (details.trajectory, details.location)
            last = self._last_location
            location_moved = (
                config.location_epsilon is not None
                and last is not None
                and last[0] == location[0]
                and abs(location[1] - last[1]) > config.location_epsilon
            )
            self._last_location = location

        joints = _joints(state)
        if joints is not None:
            last_joints = self._last_joints
            joints_moved = (
                config.joint_epsilon is not None
                and last_joints is not None
                and len(last_joints) == len(joints)
                and max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(joints, last_joints)) > config.joint_epsilon
            )
            self._last_joints = joints

        return location_moved, joints_moved

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

input.command:
git add nova/actions/container.py nova/cell/motion_group.py nova/cell/movement_controller/ nova/cell/trajectory_executor.py tests/cell/test_robust_execution.py tests/cell/test_standstill_estimator.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(cell): prove a start was taken up by commanded progress; per-unit joint thresholds

On the real cell (combined_loop, >85 % playback) the rail's operation of a
synchronized leg completed at location 0.0 before the rail moved: its encoder
noise at rest exceeded the single 1e-3 joint threshold, which was meant in rad
but compared in mm for the prismatic rail. The noise counted as corroborated
motion, the parked frames concluded paused(USER), and the ensemble returned
while the rail was still settling, so the next leg's initialize was rejected.

- In armed, PAUSED_BY_USER at standstill is a pause only once the commanded
  location has left the one the start found (same trajectory), or when a pause
  was requested. The commanded location advances only once the controller
  executes the start, so no standstill flicker can conclude a pause before it,
  with any standstill configuration. A frame of another trajectory re-anchors.
- Joint evidence is compared per unit: joint_epsilon (rad, revolute) and
  prismatic_joint_epsilon (mm, prismatic, robust default 0.1). Joint types come
  from the motion group's DH parameters, read once per MotionGroup; unknown
  types disable joint evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3
